title.zh: 卷一百六十二 列傳第八十七 姚獨孤顧韋段呂許薛李
title.en: Volume 162 Biographies 87: Yao, Du, Gu, Gu, Wei, Duan, Lu, Xu, Xue, Li
title.raw: 卷一百六十二 列傳第八十七 姚獨孤顧韋段呂許薛李 Volume 162 Biographies 87: Yao, Du, Gu, Gu, Wei, Duan, Lu, Xu, Xue, Li

sentences.zh: 姚獨孤顧韋段呂許薛李

translations.literal: Yao, Du-Gu, Gu, Wei, Duan, Lu, Xu, Xue, Li
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yao, Dugu, Gu, Wei, Duan, Lu, Xu, Xue, and Li

sentences.zh: 姚南仲，華州下邽人。

translations.literal: Yao Nanzhong was a man of Xiaji in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nanzhong came from Xiaji in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，擢制科，授太子校書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he was selected through the special examination and appointed collator to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special civil-service examination and was named collator in the heir apparent's library.

sentences.zh: 遷累右補闕。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached the post of Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to become Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，獨孤皇后崩，代宗悼痛，詔近城為陵，以朝夕臨望。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali, Empress Du Gu died. Emperor Daizong grieved deeply and ordered a tomb built near the city so he could visit morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 10 Empress Dugu passed away. Grieving deeply, Emperor Daizong commanded that a mausoleum be built near the capital so he could look in on it morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 南仲上疏曰：「臣聞人臣宅於家，帝王宅於國。

translations.literal: Nanzhong submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that subjects make their dwelling in the home, while emperors make their dwelling in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong memorialized the throne: "I have heard it said that a subject makes his home in his household, while a sovereign makes his home in the state.

sentences.zh: 長安乃祖宗所宅，其可興鑿建陵其側乎？

translations.literal: Chang'an is where our ancestors dwelt—how can we open excavations and build a tomb beside it?
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an is the dwelling of our imperial forebears—how can we carve out a burial mound right beside it?

sentences.zh: 夫葬者，藏也，欲人之不得見也。

translations.literal: Burial means concealment; one wishes that people not see the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Burial means hiding the dead away; the point is that people should not see them.

sentences.zh: 今西近宮闕，南迫大道。

translations.literal: As planned it would lie west close to the palace gates and south pressing on the main avenue.
translations.idiomatic: As planned, the site would lie west of the palace and south against the main thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 使近而可視，歿而復生，雖宮以待之可也。

translations.literal: If it is made near enough to be seen, and if the dead could return to life, one might as well build a palace to await them.
translations.idiomatic: If the tomb is placed so near that it can be seen at a glance, one might as well set up a palace and wait there, as though the dead might rise again.

sentences.zh: 如令骨肉歸土，魂無不之，雖欲自近，了復何益？

translations.literal: If flesh and bone return to earth and the soul has nowhere it does not go, even if one wishes to draw near, what use is that in the end?
translations.idiomatic: Once flesh and bone are committed to earth and the spirit roams everywhere, drawing the tomb closer gains nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 且王者必據高明，燭幽隱，先皇所以因龍首而建望春也。

translations.literal: Moreover, a king must occupy a lofty position to illuminate what is hidden—this is why the late emperor built Wangchun atop Longshou.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must sit on high ground to shed light on what lies in shadow—that is why the late emperor built Wangchun Terrace on Longshou Hill.

sentences.zh: 今起陵目前，心一感傷，累日不能平。

translations.literal: Now, raising a tomb before one's eyes, the heart is stirred to grief and cannot be settled for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: To raise a tomb before your eyes will stir grief anew day after day and leave your heart unsettled.

sentences.zh: 且匹夫向隅，滿堂不樂，況萬乘乎，天下謂何？

translations.literal: Moreover, when a common man faces a corner, the whole hall is not at ease—how much more the lord of ten thousand chariots? What would the realm say?
translations.idiomatic: When one man turns to a dark corner, the whole room falls silent; how much more when the Son of Heaven grieves openly—what would the empire think?

sentences.zh: 陛下謚後以貞懿，而終以褻近，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty gave the late empress the posthumous epithet Chaste and Admirable, yet in the end would keep her with intimate nearness—I am privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty gave the late empress the epithet Chaste and Admirable, yet would keep her remains immodestly close—I find this puzzling.

sentences.zh: 今國人皆曰後陵在邇，陛下將日省而時望焉，斯有損聖德，無益先後，欲寵反辱，惟陛下孰計。」

translations.literal: Now the people all say the empress's tomb is near and Your Majesty will daily visit and often look out upon it—this injures sagely virtue, helps neither the living nor the dead, and turns intended honor into disgrace. I beg Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Now the people all say the empress's tomb is near and Your Majesty will daily visit and often look out upon it—this injures sagely virtue, helps neither the living nor the dead, and turns intended honor into disgrace. I beg Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝嘉納，進五品階以酬讜言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it, promoting him one step in the fifth rank to reward his straightforward words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed the memorial and raised Nanzhong one rank in the fifth-grade sequence to reward his frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 坐善宰相常袞，出為海鹽令。

translations.literal: Because he was on good terms with Chief Minister Chang Gun, he was sent out as magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His association with Chief Minister Chang Gun cost him his post at court, and he was sent out as magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使韓滉表為推官，擢殿中侍御史內供奉。

translations.literal: Han Huang, commissioner for Zhexi, recommended him as legal aide; he was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor within the inner service.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, the Zhexi observation commissioner, recommended him as a legal aide, and he was promoted to an attendant imperial censor on inner duty.

sentences.zh: 召還，四遷為御史中丞，改給事中、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was promoted four times to Vice Censor-in-Chief, then changed to Supervisor of Attendants and commissioner for Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he advanced through four promotions to Vice Censor-in-Chief, then became Supervisor of Attendants and observation commissioner for Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 拜義成節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍恃權橈政，不能逞，因毀南仲於朝，德宗惑之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Xue Yingzhen relied on power to bend government affairs; Nanzhong could not let him have his way, so Yingzhen slandered Nanzhong at court, and Emperor Dezong was misled.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Xue Yingzhen abused his authority to meddle in government, and Nanzhong would not yield. Yingzhen therefore slandered him at court, and Emperor Dezong was taken in.

sentences.zh: 俄遣小使程務盈誣表以罪。

translations.literal: Before long a minor envoy, Cheng Wuying, was sent with a false memorial accusing him of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a minor envoy named Cheng Wuying was dispatched bearing a fabricated memorial that accused Nanzhong of crimes.

sentences.zh: 會南仲裨將曹文洽入奏，知其語，則晨夜追至長樂驛，及之，與同舍，夜殺務盈，投其誣於廁。

translations.literal: It happened that Nanzhong's deputy general Cao Wenqia came to court to report and learned of this; he then pursued day and night to Changle Post, caught up with him, lodged in the same quarters, killed Wuying by night, and threw the false accusation into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong's deputy general Cao Wenqia happened to be at court and learned of the plot. He pursued Cheng Wuying day and night to Changle Post, caught up with him, shared his lodging, killed him in the night, and threw the forged accusation into the latrine.

sentences.zh: 為二書，一抵南仲，一治南仲冤，且自言殺務盈狀，乃自殺。

translations.literal: He wrote two letters, one delivered to Nanzhong and one petitioning to redress Nanzhong's injustice, in which he also confessed that he had killed Wuying, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote two letters—one for Nanzhong and one petitioning the throne to clear Nanzhong's name—in which he confessed to killing Wuying, then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 驛吏以聞，帝駭異。

translations.literal: The post-station clerk reported it, and the emperor was startled.
translations.idiomatic: When the post-station clerk reported what had happened, the emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 南仲不自安，固請入朝。

translations.literal: Nanzhong was ill at ease and firmly requested to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Nanzhong urgently asked permission to return to court.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「盈珍橈卿政邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "Did Yingzhen bend your government affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, saying: "Did Yingzhen bend your government affairs?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不橈臣政，臣隳陛下法耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "He did not bend my government affairs; I merely destroyed Your Majesty's laws.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He did not interfere with my administration—I merely undermined Your Majesty's laws.

sentences.zh: 如盈珍輩，所在有之，雖使羊、杜復生，撫百姓，禦三軍，必不能成愷悌之化而正師律也。」

translations.literal: Men like Yingzhen exist everywhere. Even if Yang Hu and Du Yu were reborn to comfort the people and command the three armies, they could surely not achieve a transformation of kindness and correct military discipline."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yingzhen exist everywhere. Even if Yang Hu and Du Yu were reborn to comfort the people and command the three armies, they could surely not achieve a transformation of kindness and correct military discipline."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃授尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年卒，年七十五，贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age seventy-five; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan year 19 at the age of seventy-five. Posthumously he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the epithet Upright.

sentences.zh: 初，崔位、馬少微者，俱在南仲幕府。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Wei and Ma Shaowei had both served on Nanzhong's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Wei and Ma Shaowei had both served on Nanzhong's staff.

sentences.zh: 盈珍之譖也，出位為遂州別駕。

translations.literal: Because of Yingzhen's slander, Wei was sent out as assistant prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yingzhen's slander, Wei was sent out as assistant prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 東川觀察使王叔邕希旨奏位，殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Shuyong, commissioner for Dongchuan, eager to please, memorialized against Wei and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuyong, the Dongchuan observation commissioner, eager to please his superiors, memorialized against Wei and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 復出少微補外，使宦官護送，度江，投之水雲。

translations.literal: Shaowei was again sent out to fill an outside post; eunuchs were made to escort him. When they crossed the river, they threw him into the misty waters.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was again sent out on an external appointment, with eunuchs assigned to escort him. When they crossed the river, they threw him into the waters.

sentences.zh: 獨孤及，字至之，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Du Gu, courtesy name Zhizhi, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu, whose courtesy name was Zhizhi, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，讀《孝經》，父試之曰：「兒誌何語？」

translations.literal: As a child he read the Classic of Filial Piety. His father tested him, saying: "What lines do you remember, my boy?"
translations.idiomatic: As a child he read the Classic of Filial Piety. His father tested him, saying: "What lines do you remember, my boy?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「立身行道，揚名於後世。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Establish oneself in conduct and walk the Way, making one's name known to later ages."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Establish oneself in conduct and walk the Way, making one's name known to later ages."

sentences.zh: 宗黨奇之。

translations.literal: His clan marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen were astonished.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，以道舉高第補華陰尉，辟江淮都統李亙府，掌書記。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the Daoist learning examination with high marks and was appointed aide of Huayin; he was recruited to the staff of Li Gen, overall commander of Jianghuai, as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era he passed the Daoist learning examination with high honors and was appointed aide of Huayin. He was then recruited to the staff of Li Gen, overall commander of Jianghuai, as secretary.

sentences.zh: 代宗以左拾遺召，既至，上疏陳政曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong summoned him as Left Reminder. Once he arrived, he submitted a memorial setting forth policy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong summoned him as Left Reminder. On reaching court he submitted a memorial on state affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下屢發德音，使左右侍臣得直言極諫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has repeatedly issued virtuous pronouncements, allowing attendants at your side to speak frankly and remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has repeatedly issued benevolent edicts allowing those at your side to speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve.

sentences.zh: 壬辰詔書，召裴冕等十有三人集賢殿待制，以備詢問。

translations.literal: In the renchen edict of that year, Pei Mian and thirteen others were summoned to await imperial orders in the Jixian Hall to be ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: By the renchen edict Your Majesty summoned Pei Mian and thirteen others to await orders in the Jixian Hall, ready to answer your questions.

sentences.zh: 此五帝盛德也。

translations.literal: This is the great virtue of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the great virtue of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 然頃者陛下雖容其直，而不錄其言，所上封皆寢不報。

translations.literal: Yet recently Your Majesty, though tolerating their frankness, has not recorded their words; all sealed memorials submitted have lain dormant without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, though Your Majesty has tolerated frank speech, you have not acted on it; sealed memorials lie unanswered.

sentences.zh: 有容下之名，無聽諫之實，遂使諫者稍稍自鉗口，飽食相招為祿仕，此忠鯁之人所以竊嘆，而臣亦恥之。

translations.literal: There is a name for tolerating subordinates but no reality of heeding remonstrance, so remonstrators gradually clamp their own mouths shut and, well fed, invite one another to pursue salary and office. This is why loyal and upright men sigh in private—and I too am ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: You have the reputation of tolerating subordinates but not the reality of heeding remonstrance, so remonstrators gradually fall silent and, well fed, invite one another to pursue salary and office. That is why loyal and upright men sigh in private—and I am ashamed as well.

sentences.zh: 十室之邑，必有忠信，況朝廷之大，卿大夫之眾，陛下選授之精歟！

translations.literal: In a hamlet of ten households there must be loyal and trustworthy men—how much more in the vast court, with its multitude of ministers and grandees, if Your Majesty's selection and appointment are refined!
translations.idiomatic: In a hamlet of ten households there must be loyal and trustworthy men—how much more in this vast court with its multitude of ministers, if Your Majesty's appointments are truly discerning!

sentences.zh: 假令不能如文王之多士，其中豈不有溫故知新，可懋陳政要而億則屢中者？

translations.literal: Even if they cannot equal King Wen's many scholars, among them are there not men who review the old and know the new, who could earnestly set forth essentials of government and whose counsel would repeatedly hit the mark?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they cannot equal King Wen's many scholars, surely among them are men who review the past and grasp the new, who could earnestly set forth essentials of government and whose counsel would repeatedly prove sound?

sentences.zh: 陛下議政之際，曾不采其一說，堯之疇咨，禹之昌言，豈若是邪？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty deliberates on government, you have never adopted a single proposal of theirs. Would Yao's consultations and Yu's excellent words have been like this?
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty deliberates on government, you have never adopted a single proposal. Would Yao's consultations and Yu's excellent words have been treated so?

sentences.zh: 昔堯設謗木於五達之衢，孔子曰：「以能問於不能，以多問於寡。」

translations.literal: Formerly Yao set up a criticism board at the crossroads of five thoroughfares. Confucius said: "The able should ask the unable; the many should ask the few."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yao set up a criticism board at the crossroads of five thoroughfares. Confucius said: "The able should ask the unable; the many should ask the few."

sentences.zh: 然則多聞闕疑，不恥下問，聖人之心也。

translations.literal: Thus to hear much, leave what is doubtful in doubt, and not be ashamed to ask those below—such is the mind of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: To hear widely, leave what is doubtful in doubt, and not be ashamed to ask those below—such is the mind of the sage.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以堯、孔心為心，日降清問，其不可者罷之，可者議於朝，與執事者共之。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take the minds of Yao and Confucius as your mind, daily issuing clear inquiries; what cannot stand should be dismissed, what can stand should be debated at court and shared with those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to take the minds of Yao and Confucius as your own, to issue clear inquiries daily, to dismiss what will not do, and to debate at court what will do, sharing counsel with those in charge.

sentences.zh: 使知之必言，言之必行，行之必公，則君臣無私論，朝廷無私政，陛下以此辨可否於獻替，而建太平之階可也。

translations.literal: Let those who know speak without fail, what is spoken be carried out without fail, and what is carried out be done with public justice—then ruler and ministers will have no private opinions and the court no private policies. Your Majesty may thereby distinguish what is feasible and what is not in proposals for change and removal, and the steps to great peace may be built.
translations.idiomatic: Let those who know speak without fail, let what is spoken be carried out, and let what is carried out be just—then ruler and ministers will harbor no private designs and the court no private policies. By this Your Majesty may judge what to adopt and what to reject, and the steps to great peace may be laid.

sentences.zh: 師興不息十年矣，人之生產，空於杼軸。

translations.literal: Armies have been raised without cease for ten years; the people's production has been emptied at the loom.
translations.idiomatic: Armies have been raised without cease for ten years, and the people's production has been drained away at the loom.

sentences.zh: 擁兵者第館亙街陌，奴婢厭酒肉，而貧人羸餓就役，剝膚及髓。

translations.literal: Those who hold armies have mansions stretching across streets and lanes; their slaves and maidservants are sated with wine and meat, while the poor, emaciated and starving, go to labor and have skin and marrow flayed away.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold armies have mansions stretching block after block; their slaves are sated with wine and meat, while the poor, emaciated and starving, are pressed into service until skin and marrow are stripped away.

sentences.zh: 長安城中，白晝椎剽，吏不敢詰。

translations.literal: In the city of Chang'an, robbers strike by daylight, and clerks dare not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an, robbers strike by broad daylight, and officials dare not investigate.

sentences.zh: 官亂職廢，將墮卒暴，百揆隳剌，如沸粥紛麻。

translations.literal: Offices are in disorder and duties abandoned; generals fall and soldiers run wild; the hundred ministries are ruined and pierced, like boiling porridge tangled with hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Offices are in disorder and duties abandoned; generals fall and soldiers run wild; the hundred ministries lie in ruins, tangled like boiling porridge and hemp.

sentences.zh: 民不敢訴於有司，有司不敢聞陛下，茹毒飲痛，窮而無告。

translations.literal: The people dare not appeal to the authorities; the authorities dare not report to Your Majesty. They swallow poison and drink pain, driven to extremity with no one to tell.
translations.idiomatic: The people dare not appeal to the authorities; the authorities dare not report to Your Majesty. They swallow poison and drink pain, driven to extremity with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 今其心颙颙，獨恃於麥，麥不登，則易子咬骨矣。

translations.literal: Now their hearts look up in hope, relying solely on the wheat crop; if the wheat does not ripen, they will exchange children and gnaw bones.
translations.idiomatic: Now their hearts look up in hope, relying solely on the wheat harvest; if the wheat fails, they will exchange children and gnaw bones.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以此時厲精更始，思所以救之之術，忍令宗廟有累卵之危，萬姓悼心失圖，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not at this time exert your spirit and make a new beginning, thinking on the means to save them, but would bear the ancestral temples to have the peril of piled eggs and the myriad people to lose heart in grief with no plan—I am truly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not at this moment exert yourself and make a new beginning, thinking how to save them, but would let the ancestral temples face peril as fragile as piled eggs and the myriad people lose heart in grief with no plan—I am truly afraid.

sentences.zh: 去年十一月丁巳夜，星隕如雨，昨清明降霜，三月苦熱，錯繆顛倒，沴莫大焉。

translations.literal: On the dingsi night of the eleventh month last year, stars fell like rain; yesterday at Qingming frost descended; in the third month bitter heat—things are perverse and upside down; no calamitous sign is greater.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi night of the eleventh month last year stars fell like rain; yesterday at Qingming frost fell; in the third month came bitter heat—things are perverse and upside down, and no omen of calamity is greater.

sentences.zh: 此下陵上替，怨讟之氣取之也。

translations.literal: This comes from inferiors overbearing superiors and superiors declining—taken from the qi of resentment and complaint.
translations.idiomatic: This comes from inferiors overbearing their superiors and superiors declining—the breath of resentment and complaint.

sentences.zh: 天意丁寧譴戒，以警陛下，宜反躬罪己，旁求賢良者而師友之，黜貪佞不肖者，下哀痛之詔，去天下疾苦，廢無用之官，罷不急之費，禁止暴兵，節用愛人，兢兢乾乾，以僥福於上下，必能使天感神應，反妖災為和氣矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent is earnest admonition and warning to alert Your Majesty. You should turn inward and blame yourself, broadly seek worthy and good men to take as teachers and friends, dismiss the greedy, fawning, and unworthy, issue an edict of grief and pain, remove the sufferings of the realm, abolish useless offices, cut expenditures that are not urgent, forbid violent troops, economize and cherish the people, be cautious and diligent, and thereby seek blessing for above and below—surely Heaven will be moved and spirits respond, and evil portents and disasters be turned into harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent is earnest warning to alert Your Majesty. Turn inward and blame yourself, seek worthy men far and wide to take as teachers and friends, dismiss the greedy and fawning, issue an edict of grief and compassion, remove the realm's sufferings, abolish useless offices, cut nonessential expenditures, forbid violent troops, economize and cherish the people, and be cautious and diligent in seeking blessing for above and below—surely Heaven will be moved, spirits will respond, and evil portents will turn to harmony.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 減江淮、山南諸道兵以贍國用，陛下初不以臣言為愚，然許即施行，及今未有沛然之詔，臣竊遲之。

translations.literal: Reduce the armies of Jianghuai, Shannan, and the various circuits to support state expenses. Your Majesty at first did not regard my words as foolish and promised immediate implementation, yet to this day there has been no sweeping edict—I privately delay in hope.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the armies of Jianghuai, Shannan, and the other circuits to support state expenses. Your Majesty at first did not think my words foolish and promised immediate action, yet to this day no sweeping edict has come—I wait in private hope.

sentences.zh: 今天下唯朔方、隴西有吐蕃、仆固之虞，邠、涇、鳳翔兵足以當之矣。

translations.literal: Now in the realm only Shuofang and Longxi have concern from Tibetans and Pugu; the armies of Bin, Jing, and Fengxiang are sufficient to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Today only Shuofang and Longxi face threats from Tibetans and the Pugu; the armies of Bin, Jing, and Fengxiang are sufficient to meet them.

sentences.zh: 自此而往，東洎海，南至番禺，西盡巴蜀，無鼠竊之盜，而兵不為解。

translations.literal: From here east to the sea, south to Panyu, west to the end of Ba-Shu, there are no thieves so small as mice, yet the armies are not disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: From here east to the sea, south to Panyu, west through Ba-Shu, there are no thieves even as small as mice, yet the armies are not disbanded.

sentences.zh: 傾天下之貨，竭天下之谷，以給不用之軍，為無端之費，臣不知其故。

translations.literal: The goods of the realm are poured out and its grain exhausted to supply armies that are not needed, for expenditures without cause—I do not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The goods of the realm are poured out and its grain exhausted to supply armies that are not needed, for expenditures without cause—I do not understand why.

sentences.zh: 假令居安思危，以備不虞，自可阨害之地，俾置屯禦，悉休其餘，以糧儲扉屨之資充疲人貢賦，歲可以減國租半。

translations.literal: Even if one dwells in security and thinks of danger to prepare for the unforeseen, one may simply in perilous places set garrisons for defense and rest all the rest, using resources for grain stores and sandals to meet the tribute levies of the weary people—each year the state land tax could be reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one dwells in security and thinks of danger, one may simply post garrisons in perilous places and rest all the rest, using grain stores and humble supplies to meet the tribute levies of the weary people—each year the state land tax could be cut in half.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈遲疑於改作，逡巡於舊貫，使大議有所壅，而率土之患日甚一日？

translations.literal: Would Your Majesty delay and hesitate over reform, linger in old practices, let great deliberations be blocked, and the sufferings of all within the realm grow worse day by day?
translations.idiomatic: Would Your Majesty delay reform, cling to old practices, let great deliberations be blocked, and the sufferings of the realm grow worse day by day?

sentences.zh: 是益其弊而厚其疾也。

translations.literal: This would increase the harm and thicken the disease.
translations.idiomatic: That would only increase the harm and thicken the disease.

sentences.zh: 夫療癰者，必決之使潰。

translations.literal: In treating a carbuncle, one must lance it and make it burst.
translations.idiomatic: To treat a carbuncle, one must lance it and make it burst.

sentences.zh: 今兵之為患，猶癰也，不以漸戢之，其害滋大，大而圖之，必力倍而功寡，豈《易》「不俟終日」之義邪？

translations.literal: Now the harm of the armies is like a carbuncle; if they are not gradually reduced, the harm grows greater. To plan when it is already great, effort must be doubled while achievement is slight—is this not contrary to the meaning in the Changes, "do not wait for the whole day"?
translations.idiomatic: The harm of the armies is like a carbuncle; if they are not gradually reduced, the harm grows greater. To act only when it is already great requires double the effort for half the result—is this not contrary to the Changes' teaching, "do not wait for the whole day"?

sentences.zh: 俄改太常博士。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 或言景皇帝不宜為太祖，及據禮條上。

translations.literal: Some said Emperor Jing should not serve as Grand Ancestor, and he submitted a memorial citing ritual provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When some argued that Emperor Jing should not serve as Grand Ancestor, he submitted a memorial citing the ritual provisions.

sentences.zh: 謚呂諲、盧弈、郭知運等無浮美，無隱惡，得褒貶之正。

translations.literal: In assigning posthumous titles to Lu Yin, Lu Yi, Guo Zhiyun, and others, he used no inflated praise and hid no evil—he attained the correctness of praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: In assigning posthumous titles to Lu Yin, Lu Yi, Guo Zhiyun, and others, he used no inflated praise and hid no evil, achieving the proper balance of praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部員外郎，歷濠、舒二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and served successively as prefect of Hao and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and served successively as prefect of Hao and Shu.

sentences.zh: 歲饑旱，鄰郡庸亡什四以上，舒人獨安。

translations.literal: In a year of famine and drought, in neighboring prefectures more than four-tenths of corvée laborers perished, while the people of Shu alone remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine and drought, neighboring prefectures lost more than four-tenths of their corvée laborers, while the people of Shu alone remained secure.

sentences.zh: 以治課加檢校司封郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: For excellence in administration he was given the additional title of Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments and awarded gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: For excellence in administration he was given the additional title of Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments and awarded gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 徙常州，甘露降其廷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Changzhou; sweet dew descended in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Changzhou, where sweet dew descended in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十三，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-three; his posthumous title was Admonitory.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-three and was given the posthumous epithet Admonitory.

sentences.zh: 及喜鑒拔後進，如梁肅、高參、崔元翰、陳京、唐次、齊抗皆師事之。

translations.literal: Gu delighted in discerning and promoting younger men; Liang Su, Gao Can, Cui Yuanhan, Chen Jing, Tang Ci, and Qi Kang all took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Gu delighted in discerning and promoting younger men; Liang Su, Gao Can, Cui Yuanhan, Chen Jing, Tang Ci, and Qi Kang all studied under him.

sentences.zh: 性孝友。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and friendly.

sentences.zh: 其為文彰明善惡，長於論議。

translations.literal: His writing made good and evil manifest and excelled in discourse and argument.
translations.idiomatic: His writing made good and evil manifest and excelled in discourse and argument.

sentences.zh: 晚嗜琴，有眼疾，不肯治，欲聽之專也。

translations.literal: In his later years he loved the zither; he had an eye ailment but refused treatment, wishing to devote himself wholly to listening.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he loved the zither; he had an eye ailment but refused treatment, wishing to devote himself wholly to listening.

sentences.zh: 子朗、郁。

translations.literal: His sons were Lang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Lang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 朗，字用晦，由處士辟署江西、宣歙、浙東三府。

translations.literal: Lang, courtesy name Yonghui, was recruited from private life to serve in the staffs of Jiangxi, Xuan-She, and Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang, whose courtesy name was Yonghui, was recruited from private life to serve on the staffs of Jiangxi, Xuan-She, and Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 元和中，擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 建言：「宜用觀察使領本道鹽鐵，罷場監管榷吏，除百姓之患。」

translations.literal: He offered counsel: "The observation commissioner should be used to oversee this circuit's salt and iron, the field supervisors who monopolize and tax should be abolished, and the people's affliction removed."
translations.idiomatic: He offered counsel: "The observation commissioner should be used to oversee this circuit's salt and iron, the field supervisors who monopolize and tax should be abolished, and the people's affliction removed."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 盜殺武元衡，朗請貶京兆尹，誅捕賊吏。

translations.literal: When bandits killed Wu Yuanheng, Lang requested that the metropolitan magistrate be demoted and the officers who failed to capture the bandits be punished.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits killed Wu Yuanheng, Lang requested that the metropolitan magistrate be demoted and the officers who failed to capture the killers be punished.

sentences.zh: 因勸罷兵，忤憲宗意，貶興元戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Because he urged disbanding the armies and offended Emperor Xianzong's intent, he was demoted to revenue adjutant of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because he urged disbanding the armies and offended Emperor Xianzong, he was demoted to revenue adjutant of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 久乃拜殿中侍御史，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and concurrently compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and concurrently compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 坐與李景儉飲，景儉使酒慢宰相，出為韶州刺史。

translations.literal: Because he drank with Li Jingjian, and Jingjian, drunk, insulted the chief minister, he was sent out as prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he drank with Li Jingjian, who when drunk insulted the chief minister, Lang was sent out as prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，再遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was promoted twice to Grand Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted twice to Grand Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，宦官毆鄠令崔發雞幹下，朗請誅首惡以正常法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingzong's reign, eunuchs beat Magistrate Cui Fa of E below Jigan; Lang requested that the chief culprits be executed to restore normal law.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingzong's reign, eunuchs beat Magistrate Cui Fa of E below Jigan; Lang requested that the chief culprits be executed to restore the rule of law.

sentences.zh: 王播賂權近，還判鹽鐵，朗連疏論執。

translations.literal: Wang Bo bribed those near power and returned to oversee salt and iron; Lang submitted successive memorials arguing against it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo bribed those near power and returned to oversee salt and iron; Lang submitted successive memorials arguing against the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 故事，選御史皆中丞自請。

translations.literal: By precedent, the selection of censors was entirely at the vice censor-in-chief's own nomination.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding practice, the vice censor-in-chief alone nominated candidates for censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 是時，崔晁、鄭居中繇宰相力得監察御史，朗拒不納，晁、居中卒改他官。

translations.literal: At that time, Cui Chao and Zheng Juzhong had obtained appointments as investigative censors through the chief minister's power; Lang refused to accept them, and Chao and Juzhong in the end were changed to other offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Chao and Zheng Juzhong had secured appointments as investigative censors through the chief minister's influence, but Lang refused to accept them, and in the end both men were assigned to other posts.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李道樞醉謁朗，朗劾不虔，下除司議郎。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Li Daoshu came to visit Lang while drunk; Lang impeached him for irreverence, and he was demoted and removed as Remonstrance Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Li Daoshu visited Lang while drunk; Lang impeached him for disrespect, and he was demoted from office to Remonstrance Secretary.

sentences.zh: 會殿中王源植貶官，朗直其枉，書五上不報，即自劾執法不稱，願罷去。

translations.literal: When Palace Attendant Wang Yuanzhi was demoted, Lang maintained that he had been wronged, submitted five memorials without response, then impeached himself for inadequacy in law enforcement and wished to resign.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Wang Yuanzhi was demoted, Lang insisted he had been wrongfully punished; after five unanswered memorials he impeached himself for failing in his duties and asked to be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人尉諭不許。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Wei Yu to instruct him that his resignation was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Wei Yu to tell him that his resignation would not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 文宗初，遷工部侍郎，出為福建觀察使，創發背卒，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wenzong's reign, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works, sent out as Military Commissioner of Fujian, developed a carbuncle on his back and died, and was posthumously awarded Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wenzong's reign he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and sent out as Military Commissioner of Fujian; a carbuncle on his back proved fatal, and he was posthumously awarded the title Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 郁，字古風，始生而孤，與朗育於伯父汜。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Gufeng, was orphaned from birth and was raised with Lang by their uncle Si.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Gufeng, lost his father at birth and was raised together with Lang by their uncle Si.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，最為權德輿所稱，以女妻之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was most praised by Quan Deyu, who gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and won high praise from Quan Deyu, who gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 元和初，舉制科高等，拜右拾遺，俄兼史館修撰，進右補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he passed the special examination with high rank, was appointed Right Remonstrance Official, soon also served as compiler at the Historiography Institute, and was promoted to Right Supplementor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he passed the special examination with high honors, was appointed Right Remonstrance Official, soon added the post of Historiography Institute compiler, and was promoted to Right Supplementor.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀討王承宗，郁執不可，挺議鯁固，號稱職。

translations.literal: When Tutu Chengcui attacked Wang Chengzong, Yu steadfastly objected; his upright memorials were firm and uncompromising, and he was acclaimed as fulfilling his duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Tutu Chengcui marched against Wang Chengzong, Yu firmly opposed the campaign; his blunt, unyielding memorials won praise for his fulfillment of office.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 德輿輔政，以嫌去內職，拜考功員外郎，仍兼修撰。

translations.literal: When Deyu entered the government, Yu left his inner-court post because of the conflict of interest, was appointed External Official of the Ministry of Personnel's Evaluation Bureau, and still concurrently served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu entered the government, Yu stepped down from his inner-court post to avoid conflict of interest, was appointed External Official of the Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel, and continued as a historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘆德輿乃有佳婿，詔宰相高選世族，故杜悰尚岐陽公主，然帝猶謂不如德輿之得郁也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong sighed that Deyu had such an excellent son-in-law, ordered the chief ministers to select high from noble clans, and so Du Cong married Princess Qiyang, yet the emperor still said it was not as good as Deyu's having Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong sighed that Deyu had such an excellent son-in-law, and ordered the chief ministers to choose sons-in-law from the highest noble families; Du Cong therefore married Princess Qiyang, yet the emperor still said none matched Deyu's match with Yu.

sentences.zh: 俄知制誥。

translations.literal: Soon he was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 德輿去位，還為學士。

translations.literal: When Deyu left office, Yu returned to being an academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu left office, Yu returned to his post as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 九年，以疾辭禁近，徙秘書少監，屏居鄠，卒，年四十，贈絳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on grounds of illness he resigned his post near the emperor, was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, lived in seclusion at E, died at age forty, and was posthumously awarded Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he resigned his inner-court post on grounds of illness, was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, retired to live in seclusion at E, died at forty, and was posthumously made Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 郁有雅名，帝遇之厚，議者亦謂當宰相，共以早世惜之。

translations.literal: Yu had a refined reputation; the emperor treated him generously; commentators also said he should have become chief minister; all regretted his early death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu enjoyed a refined reputation and received generous favor from the emperor; observers said he was destined for the chief ministership, and all mourned his early death.

sentences.zh: 子庠，字賢府，喪父始十歲，有至性，聞呼父官及吊客來，輒號慟幾絕。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, styled Xianfu, was only ten when his father died; he had exceptional filial nature; when he heard his father's official title called or when mourners came, he would wail until nearly unconscious.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, styled Xianfu, was only ten when his father died; possessed of deep filial feeling, whenever he heard his father's rank announced or mourners arrived, he would wail until he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 後舉進士，仕至尚書丞。

translations.literal: Later he passed the jinshi examination and served up to Secretary of a Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the jinshi examination and rose to serve as a secretary in one of the ministries.

sentences.zh: 顧少連，字夷仲，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Gu Shaolian, styled Yizhong, was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shaolian, styled Yizhong, was a native of Wu in Suzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，尤為禮部侍郎薛邕所器，擢上第，以拔萃補登封主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was especially valued by Vice Minister of Rites Xue Yong, placed in the top rank, and through exceptional selection was appointed Chief Clerk of Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was especially favored by Vice Minister of Rites Xue Yong, who placed him in the top rank; through exceptional selection he was appointed chief clerk of Dengfeng.

sentences.zh: 邑有虎孽，民患之，少連命塞陷阱，獨移文嶽神，虎不為害。

translations.literal: The district had a tiger causing harm; the people suffered from it; Shaolian ordered the traps filled in and wrote alone to the mountain deity; the tiger did no further harm.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger was ravaging the district and the people were in distress; Shaolian had the traps filled in and wrote a proclamation to the mountain god alone, after which the tiger did no further harm.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫於頎薦為監察御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yu Mi recommended him as Investigative Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yu Mi recommended him for appointment as investigative censor.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，徒步詣謁，授水部員外郎、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Dezong went to Fengtian, he went on foot to pay his respects and was appointed External Official of the Water Bureau and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, he went on foot to pay his respects and was appointed External Official of the Water Bureau and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書舍人，閱十年，以謹密稱。

translations.literal: He was promoted twice to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat; over ten years he was known for discretion and conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat, and over ten years earned a reputation for discretion and reliability.

sentences.zh: 嘗請徙先兆於洛，帝重遠去，詔遣其子往，且命中人護蕆葬役。

translations.literal: He once requested to move his ancestors' tombs to Luoyang; the emperor, reluctant to let him go far away, ordered his son sent in his place and commanded eunuchs to oversee the burial work.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked to move his forebears' tombs to Luoyang; the emperor, unwilling to let him leave court, ordered his son to go in his stead and sent eunuchs to supervise the burial.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡方橫，無敢忤者。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was then running rampant, and no one dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was then riding high, and no one dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與少連會田鎬第，酒酣，少連挺笏曰：「段秀實笏擊賊臣，今吾笏將擊奸臣！」

translations.literal: Once when Shaolian met at Tian Hao's residence, as the wine ran deep Shaolian drew his court tablet and said: "Duan Xiushi struck a traitorous minister with his tablet—now my tablet will strike a treacherous minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Shaolian was gathered at Tian Hao's residence and the wine had gone to their heads, Shaolian raised his court tablet and declared: "Duan Xiushi used his tablet to strike down a traitorous minister—now my tablet will strike a treacherous minister!"

sentences.zh: 奮且前，元友直在坐，歡解之。

translations.literal: He flung himself forward; Yuan Youzhi was present and repeatedly restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: He lunged forward, but Yuan Youzhi, who was present, stepped in and held him back.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬簡，不為灼灼名。

translations.literal: His administration favored leniency and simplicity; he did not seek a glaring reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His governance favored leniency and simplicity, and he did not chase a flashy reputation.

sentences.zh: 先是，京畿租賦薄厚不能一，少連以法均之。

translations.literal: Previously, land tax assessments in the capital region varied in severity and could not be uniform; Shaolian equalized them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Previously land-tax assessments in the capital region had been uneven in burden; Shaolian brought them into balance according to law.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，封本縣男，徙兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, enfeoffed as Baron of his home county, then moved to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel, enfeoffed as Baron of his home county, and then transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 為東都留守，表禁苑及汝閑田募耕以便民，閱武力，利鎧仗，號良吏。

translations.literal: As eastern capital garrison commander, he memorialized to open imperial parklands and idle fields along the Ru for tenant farming to benefit the people, reviewed military readiness, improved armor and weapons, and was acclaimed as an excellent official.
translations.idiomatic: As eastern capital garrison commander, he memorialized to open imperial parklands and idle fields along the Ru River for tenant farming to benefit the people, reviewed military strength, improved armor and weapons, and was hailed as an excellent administrator.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two, was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two, was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was given the posthumous title Jing (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 始，少連攜少子師閔奔行在，有詔同止翰林院，車駕還，授同州參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Shaolian fled with his youngest son Shi Min to the mobile court; there was an edict permitting them to lodge together in the Hanlin grounds; when the imperial carriage returned, Shi Min was appointed Army Adjutant of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Shaolian fled with his youngest son Shi Min to the mobile court; an edict allowed them to stay together in the Hanlin grounds, and when the emperor returned Shi Min was appointed army adjutant of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋夏卿，字雲客，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaqing, styled Yunke, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing, styled Yunke, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少邃於學，善文辭。

translations.literal: From youth he was deeply versed in learning and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply learned and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，與弟正卿同舉賢良方正，皆策高等。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, he and his younger brother Zhengqing both entered the Worthy and Upright examination and both ranked high in the policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he and his younger brother Zhengqing both entered the Worthy and Upright examination and both scored at the top of the policy essays.

sentences.zh: 授高陵主簿，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of Gaoling and through successive promotions became External Official of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Gaoling and rose through successive promotions to External Official of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時仍歲旱蝗，詔以郎官宰畿甸，授奉天令，課第一，改長安令。

translations.literal: When drought and locusts struck year after year, an edict ordered bureau officials to administer the capital region; he was appointed Magistrate of Fengtian, ranked first in assessment, and was transferred to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and locusts afflicted the region year after year, an edict sent bureau officials to govern the capital districts; he was appointed magistrate of Fengtian, ranked first in assessment, and was then made magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部員外郎、郎中，擢給事中，出為常、蘇二州刺史。

translations.literal: He moved on to External Official and then Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was promoted to Censor in Attendance, and was sent out as Prefect of Chang and Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as External Official and then Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was promoted to Censor in Attendance, and was sent out as prefect of Changzhou and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐州節度使張建封疾甚，詔夏卿為徐泗行軍司馬，且代之。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou was gravely ill; Xiaqing was ordered to serve as campaign deputy commander of Xu-Si and to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, military commissioner of Xuzhou, fell gravely ill; Xiaqing was ordered to serve as campaign deputy commander of Xu-Si and to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 未至，而建封卒，徐軍立其子愔為留後，召夏卿為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Jianfeng died; the Xu army enthroned his son Yin as acting commander; Xiaqing was recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Jianfeng died; the Xu army installed his son Yin as acting commander, and Xiaqing was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時從弟執誼在翰林，嘗受人金，有所幹請，密以金內夏卿懷中，夏卿毀懷不受，曰：「吾與爾賴先人遺德，致位及此，顧當是哉？」

translations.literal: At the time his younger cousin Zhuyi was in the Hanlin Academy; he had once received someone's gold to make a request and secretly put the gold into Xiaqing's bosom; Xiaqing tore it open and refused to accept, saying: "You and I owe our offices to our forebears' legacy—how could this be right?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger cousin Zhuyi was in the Hanlin Academy; having once taken gold from someone to press a request, he secretly slipped the gold into Xiaqing's robe; Xiaqing tore it open and refused it, saying: "You and I owe our positions to our ancestors' legacy—how could we do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 執誼大慚。

translations.literal: Zhuyi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 轉京兆尹、太子賓客，檢校工部尚書，為東都留守，辭疾，改太子少保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Jingzhao and Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, acting as Minister of Works, served as eastern capital garrison commander, pleaded illness, and was changed to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Magistrate of Jingzhao and Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with acting appointment as Minister of Works, served as eastern capital garrison commander, pleaded illness, and was reassigned as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰獻。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-four, was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was given the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four, was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was given the posthumous title Xian (Dedicated).

sentences.zh: 夏卿性通簡，好古有遠韻，談說多聞。

translations.literal: Xiaqing's nature was open and unpretentious; he loved antiquity and had a far-reaching elegance; in conversation he was widely informed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing was open and unpretentious by nature; he loved antiquity and had a refined, far-reaching sensibility, and in conversation he was remarkably well informed.

sentences.zh: 晚歲將罷歸，署其居曰「大隱洞」。

translations.literal: In his later years, about to retire and return home, he inscribed his residence with the name "Great Recluse Cave."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, about to retire and return home, he inscribed his residence with the name "Great Recluse Cave."

sentences.zh: 與齊映、穆贊、贊弟員友善，雖同遊，終年不見其喜怛。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Qi Ying, Mu Zan, and Zan's younger brother Yuan. Though they traveled together, throughout the year one never saw him show joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Qi Ying, Mu Zan, and Zan's younger brother Yuan. Even when they traveled together, one could spend a whole year with him and never see a flash of joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 撫孤侄恩逾己子。

translations.literal: He raised his orphaned nephew with affection exceeding that shown to his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his orphaned nephew with a devotion that surpassed what he gave his own sons.

sentences.zh: 為政務通理，不甚作條教。

translations.literal: In governing he pursued broad principle and did not greatly set down detailed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In office he sought broad, sensible governance and did not rely much on rigid rules and regulations.

sentences.zh: 所辟士如路隋、張賈、李景儉等，至宰相達官，故世稱知人。

translations.literal: Among the scholars he recruited, such as Lu Sui, Zhang Jia, and Li Jingjian, many rose to chancellorship and high office; therefore the age praised him for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars he brought into service, such as Lu Sui, Zhang Jia, and Li Jingjian, went on to become chancellors and high officials, so his contemporaries hailed him as a man who knew talent.

sentences.zh: 正卿子瓘，字茂弘，及進士第，仕累中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhengqing's son Guan, styled Maohong, passed the jinshi examination and through service rose to Chief Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengqing's son Guan, styled Maohong, passed the jinshi examination and eventually rose to become a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與李德裕善，德裕任宰相，罕接士，唯瓘往請無間也。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Li Deyu. When Deyu served as chancellor he rarely received scholars, yet Guan alone called on him without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Li Deyu. Once Deyu became chancellor he rarely saw visitors, but Guan alone continued to call on him without letup.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔惡之，德裕罷，貶為明州長史。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin resented him. When Deyu was dismissed, Guan was demoted to Administrator of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin bore him ill will. After Deyu was removed from office, Guan was demoted to administrator of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會昌末，累遷楚州刺史，終桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Huichang era he rose in successive appointments to Prefect of Chu Prefecture, and ended as Military Commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Huichang reign he rose through successive posts to prefect of Chu Prefecture and ended his career as military commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 段平仲，字秉庸，本武威人，隋民部尚書達六世孫。

translations.literal: Duan Pingzhong, styled Bingyong, was originally a man of Wuwei, a sixth-generation descendant of Da, Minister of the Household in the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzhong, styled Bingyong, came from Wuwei and was a sixth-generation descendant of Da, who had served as Minister of the Household under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、李復之節度淮南，連表掌書記。

translations.literal: When Du You and Li Fuzhi served as military governors of Huainan, they repeatedly memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Du You and Li Fuzhi held command in Huainan, each repeatedly recommended him to serve as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 磊落有氣節，嗜酒敢言。

translations.literal: He was forthright and possessed moral integrity; he loved wine and dared to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: He was open and principled, fond of wine, and unafraid to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 是時，德宗春秋高，躬自聽斷，天下事有所壅隔，群臣畏帝苛察，無敢言。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Dezong was advanced in years and personally heard and decided cases. Affairs of the empire were blocked in places. The ministers feared the emperor's severe scrutiny, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Dezong was old and decided matters himself. Public business was often obstructed, and the officials, fearing his harsh scrutiny, dared not speak out.

sentences.zh: 平仲常曰：「上聰明神武，但臣下畏怯，自為循默爾。

translations.literal: Pingzhong often said: "The sovereign is intelligent and divinely martial, but the officials are fearful and timid, and so they keep silent on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong often said, "The emperor is brilliant and formidable—it is only that his ministers are timid and choose to hold their tongues.

sentences.zh: 使我一日得召見，宜大有開納。」

translations.literal: If I should one day be summoned to audience, there ought to be great openness and acceptance."
translations.idiomatic: If I should one day be summoned to audience, there ought to be great openness and acceptance."

sentences.zh: 會京師旱，詔擇御史、郎官開倉振恤。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered drought, an edict ordered that censors and directorate officials be selected to open the granaries and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the capital, an edict called for censors and directorate officials to be chosen to open the granaries and provide famine relief.

sentences.zh: 平仲與考功員外郎陳歸被選，同得對，粗陳振恤事，帝察其意有所畜，以歸在側未言。

translations.literal: Pingzhong and Chen Gui, an auxiliary director in the Ministry of Personnel, were selected. They both gained an audience and roughly set forth the relief measures. The emperor perceived that Pingzhong had something he was holding back. Because Gui was present at his side, he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong and Chen Gui, an auxiliary director in the Ministry of Personnel, were chosen. Both were granted an audience and briefly reported on the relief work. The emperor saw that Pingzhong had more on his mind, but with Chen Gui standing beside him he held back.

sentences.zh: 事訖，平仲方獨進，帝乃並留歸，正色問之，雜以它語，平仲錯牾不得言，乃謬稱名，帝怒，叱去之。

translations.literal: When the business was finished, Pingzhong alone stepped forward. The emperor then kept Gui as well, and with a stern countenance questioned him, mixing in other topics. Pingzhong, confused and contradicting himself, could not speak; he then wrongly stated his name. The emperor grew angry and shouted at him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended, Pingzhong stepped forward alone. The emperor kept Chen Gui there too and questioned him with a stern face, interspersing other subjects. Pingzhong grew flustered and contradicted himself until he could say nothing; then he even gave his name incorrectly. The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him out.

sentences.zh: 蒼黃向幄後，歸趨降招之，乃得去。

translations.literal: In confusion he turned toward the rear of the screen. Gui hurried down to beckon him, and only then was he able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Flustered, he turned toward the back of the screen. Chen Gui hurried down to signal him, and only then did he manage to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 由是坐廢七年，然名由此顯。

translations.literal: Because of this he sat idle for seven years, yet his name became famous from this incident.
translations.idiomatic: For this he languished in obscurity for seven years, yet it was this very episode that made his name known.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為諫議大夫，憲宗使吐突承璀討鎮州，亟疏爭，不可。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he served as Remonstrance Grandee. When Emperor Xianzong sent Tutu Chengcui to campaign against Zhen Prefecture, he urgently submitted memorials in opposition, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he became remonstrance grandee. When Emperor Xianzong dispatched Tutu Chengcui to attack Zhen Prefecture, Pingzhong repeatedly memorialized in protest, but to no avail.

sentences.zh: 及還，無功，又請斬之。

translations.literal: When Chengcui returned without achievement, Pingzhong again requested that he be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengcui returned without success, Pingzhong again petitioned that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Right Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice director of the right bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有得失，未嘗不論奏，世推其敢直雲。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had gains or losses, he never failed to submit memorials discussing them. The age praised his bold forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court erred or excelled, he never failed to speak out in memorials, and his contemporaries admired his fearless candor.

sentences.zh: 終太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He ended as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君有常尊，臣有定卑，自然之勢也。

translations.literal: Appreciation: The ruler has a fixed dignity, and the minister has a fixed inferiority—these are the natural order of things.
translations.idiomatic: Appreciation: The ruler holds a fixed dignity and the minister a fixed subordination—such is the natural order.

sentences.zh: 然臣不自通於上，君不降而逮諸下，則治不得成而功不彰。

translations.literal: Yet if ministers do not make themselves understood to their superiors, and the ruler does not lower himself to reach down to those below, then governance cannot succeed and achievements cannot be made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if ministers do not open communication upward and the ruler does not humble himself to reach those below, good governance cannot be achieved and merit cannot shine forth.

sentences.zh: 返是而天下之務粲焉幾矣。

translations.literal: Reverse this, and the affairs of the empire would be splendidly near completion.
translations.idiomatic: Turn this around, and the business of the empire would be brought nearly to perfection.

sentences.zh: 德宗察察，欲折伏臣下，自為聰明，而治愈疏。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was scrutinizing; he wished to subdue his ministers and considered himself clever, yet governance grew ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was hyper-vigilant. He sought to break his ministers into submission and prided himself on his own cleverness, yet the more he did so the further good governance receded.

sentences.zh: 段平仲一忤上，蒼惶失對，而猶以取名，何哉？

translations.literal: Duan Pingzhong once offended the emperor, flustered and unable to answer properly, yet still gained renown from it—how can this be?
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzhong once offended the emperor, flustered and unable to answer coherently, yet still won fame from the episode—how can that be?

sentences.zh: 下知所職，而上喪其所以為上也。

translations.literal: Those below knew their duties, while the sovereign lost what it meant to be sovereign above.
translations.idiomatic: Those below knew their place, while the ruler above lost what it meant to rule.

sentences.zh: 故聖王屈己從諫，君臣兩得其美，知道之本歟！

translations.literal: Therefore the sage king humbles himself to accept remonstrance, and ruler and minister each gain the best of it—is this not the root of the Way!
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage king humbles himself to heed remonstrance, so that ruler and minister each gain what is best—is this not the very root of the Way?

sentences.zh: 呂元膺，字景夫，鄆州東平人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanying, styled Jingfu, was a man of Dongping in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanying, styled Jingfu, came from Dongping in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姿儀瑰秀，有器識。

translations.literal: His bearing was strikingly handsome, and he possessed talent and insight.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in appearance and possessed both talent and judgment.

sentences.zh: 始遊京師，謁故宰相齊映，映嘆曰：「吾不及識婁、郝，殆斯人類乎！」

translations.literal: When he first traveled to the capital, he called on the former chancellor Qi Ying. Qi sighed and said: "I did not live long enough to know Lou and Hao—I fear this man may be of their kind!"
translations.idiomatic: When he first traveled to the capital, he called on the former chancellor Qi Ying. Qi sighed and said: "I did not live long enough to know Lou and Hao—I fear this man may be of their kind!"

sentences.zh: 策賢良高第，調安邑尉，辟長春宮判官。

translations.literal: He ranked high in the special examination for the worthy and able, was posted as magistrate of Anyi County, and was recruited as judge of the Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top of the special examination for the worthy and able, was appointed magistrate of Anyi County, and was recruited as judge of the Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 李懷光亂河中，輒解去。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong, Yuanying immediately resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong, Yuanying promptly resigned and departed.

sentences.zh: 論惟明節度渭北，表佐其府。

translations.literal: When Lun Weiming served as military governor of Weibei, he memorialized to have Yuanying assist in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun Weiming held command in Weibei, he recommended Yuanying to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 惟明卒，王棲曜代之，德宗敕棲曜留元膺自佐，入拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Weiming died, Wang Qiyao replaced him. Emperor Dezong ordered Qiyao to retain Yuanying to assist him, and Yuanying entered the capital to be appointed Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Weiming died, Wang Qiyao took his place. Emperor Dezong instructed Qiyao to keep Yuanying on as his aide, and Yuanying then entered the capital and was appointed palace censor.

sentences.zh: 歷右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as auxiliary director in the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as auxiliary director in the right bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為蘄州刺史，嘗錄囚，囚或白：「父母在，明日歲旦不得省，為恨。」

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture. Once when reviewing prisoners, a prisoner said: "My parents are alive, and tomorrow is New Year's Day—I cannot visit them, which fills me with regret."
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture. Once when reviewing prisoners, a prisoner said: "My parents are alive, and tomorrow is New Year's Day—I cannot visit them, which fills me with regret."

sentences.zh: 因泣，元膺惻然，悉釋械歸之，而戒還期。

translations.literal: He wept. Yuanying was moved with compassion, released all their shackles and sent them home, while setting a deadline for return.
translations.idiomatic: The man wept. Moved to pity, Yuanying removed all their shackles and sent them home, but set a date for their return.

sentences.zh: 吏白「不可」，答曰：「吾以信待人，人豈我違？」

translations.literal: The clerks said it was not permissible. He replied: "I treat people with trust—would they betray me?"
translations.idiomatic: The clerks protested that this could not be done. He answered, "I treat people with trust—would they betray me?"

sentences.zh: 如期而至。

translations.literal: They returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: They returned on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 自是群盜感愧，悉避境去。

translations.literal: From this the bandits in the region were moved with shame and all left the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: After this the local bandits were so moved by shame that they all left the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和中，累擢給事中。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he rose in successive appointments to Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign he rose through successive posts to become supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既謝，帝逮問政事，所對詳詣。

translations.literal: After he had taken leave of office, the emperor summoned him to question him on state affairs; his answers were detailed and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: After he had bid farewell to take up his post, the emperor summoned him back to question him on state affairs, and his replies were detailed and precise.

sentences.zh: 明日，謂宰相曰：「元膺直氣讜言，宜留左右，奈何出之？」

translations.literal: The next day he said to the chancellors: "Yuanying is upright in spirit and speaks forthright counsel. He should be kept close at hand—why send him away?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said to the chancellors: "Yuanying is upright in spirit and speaks forthright counsel. He should be kept close at hand—why send him away?"

sentences.zh: 李藩、裴垍謝，因言：「陛下及此，乃宗社無疆之休。

translations.literal: Li Fan and Pei Ji thanked him, then said: "Your Majesty reaching this point is boundless good fortune for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and Pei Ji thanked him, then added, "Your Majesty's reaching this judgment is boundless good fortune for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣等昧死請留元膺給事左右。」

translations.literal: We dare risk death to request that Yuanying be retained to serve at Your Majesty's side."
translations.idiomatic: We venture to beg that Yuanying be kept at Your Majesty's side to serve the court."

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼皇太子侍讀，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: Not long after, he was additionally made tutor to the crown prince and promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also appointed tutor to the crown prince and promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 拜鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of E-Yue.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜登城，守者不許。

translations.literal: Once at night he climbed the city wall; the guards would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at night, he tried to ascend the city wall, but the guards refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「中丞也。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "It is the Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side said: "It is the Censor-in-Chief."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夜不可辨。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "At night one cannot tell."
translations.idiomatic: The guard answered, "In the dark I cannot tell who you are."

sentences.zh: 乃還。

translations.literal: Yuanying thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying went back.

sentences.zh: 明日，擢守者為大將。

translations.literal: The next day he promoted the guard to senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he promoted that guard to senior commander.

sentences.zh: 入拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and was appointed left vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 度支使潘孟陽、太府卿王遂交相惡，乃除孟陽散騎常侍，遂鄧州刺史，詔辭無所輕重。

translations.literal: Fiscal Commissioner Pan Mengyang and Grand Provisioner Wang Sui detested each other. Thereupon Mengyang was made Regular Attendant, and Sui Prefect of Deng Prefecture—the wording of the edicts showed no distinction between right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal commissioner Pan Mengyang and grand provisioner Wang Sui hated each other. Mengyang was made regular attendant and Wang Sui prefect of Deng Prefecture, yet the edicts' language made no distinction between the worthy and the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 元膺上其詔，請明枉直，以顯褒懲。

translations.literal: Yuanying submitted the edicts and requested that right and wrong be made clear, to show reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying submitted the edicts and asked that right and wrong be made plain, so that reward and punishment would be clear.

sentences.zh: 江西裴堪按虔州刺史李將順受賕，不覆訊而貶。

translations.literal: Pei Kan of Jiangxi investigated Prefect Li Jiangshun of Qian Prefecture for accepting bribes and demoted him without a further hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kan, commissioner of Jiangxi, investigated Li Jiangshun, prefect of Qian Prefecture, for taking bribes and had him demoted without holding a rehearing.

sentences.zh: 元膺曰：「觀察使奏部刺史，不加覆，雖當誅，猶不可為天下法。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "When an observation commissioner reports on a prefect under his jurisdiction and demotes him without a rehearing, even if execution were warranted, this still cannot serve as precedent for the empire."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying said: "When an observation commissioner reports on a prefect under his jurisdiction and demotes him without a rehearing, even if execution were warranted, this still cannot serve as precedent for the empire."

sentences.zh: 請遣御史按問，宰相不能奪。

translations.literal: He requested that censors be dispatched to investigate; the chancellors could not overrule him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that censors be dispatched to investigate, and the chancellors could not overrule him.

sentences.zh: 選拜東都留守。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed Eastern Capital Defender.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and appointed defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 故事，留守賜旗甲，至元膺不給。

translations.literal: By precedent, defenders were granted banners and armor; when Yuanying took office, these were not provided.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, defenders of the capital were granted banners and armor, but when Yuanying took office none were issued.

sentences.zh: 或上言：「用兵討淮西，東都近賊，損其儀，沮威望，請比華、汝、壽三州。」

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial: "With troops deployed to campaign against Huainan West, the Eastern Capital is near the enemy. To diminish its insignia would undermine its authority. Request that it be treated like the three prefectures of Hua, Ru, and Shou."
translations.idiomatic: Someone submitted a memorial: "With troops deployed to campaign against Huainan West, the Eastern Capital is near the enemy. To diminish its insignia would undermine its authority. Request that it be treated like the three prefectures of Hua, Ru, and Shou."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，並三州罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed this, and abolished the practice for all three prefectures as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and abolished the practice for those three prefectures as well.

sentences.zh: 留守不賜旗甲，自此始。

translations.literal: Defenders no longer receiving banners and armor began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the Eastern Capital defender ceased to receive banners and armor.

sentences.zh: 都有李師道留邸，邸兵與山棚謀竊發，事覺，元膺禽破之。

translations.literal: In the capital district was Li Shidao's liaison residence; the residence troops plotted with the Mountain Sheds to launch a surprise attack. When the plot was discovered, Yuanying captured and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital district stood a liaison residence maintained by Li Shidao. Its garrison soldiers conspired with the Mountain Sheds to launch a surprise uprising. When the plot was exposed, Yuanying captured the conspirators and broke up the scheme.

sentences.zh: 始，盜發，都人震恐，守兵弱不足恃，元膺坐城門指縱部分，意氣閑舒，人賴以安。

translations.literal: At first, when the plot broke out, the people of the capital were shaken with fear. The garrison was weak and could not be relied upon. Yuanying sat at the city gate directing and deploying the troops, his bearing calm and at ease, and the people depended on this for peace of mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot first came to light, the people of the capital were terrified. The garrison was too weak to be trusted. Yuanying took his seat at the city gate, directing the deployment of forces with calm and unhurried bearing, and the people drew reassurance from him.

sentences.zh: 東畿西南通鄧、虢，川谷曠深，多麋鹿，人業射獵而不事農，遷徙無常，皆趫悍善鬥，號曰「山棚」。

translations.literal: Southwest of the Eastern Capital jurisdiction, connecting with Deng and Guo, the valleys and ravines were broad and deep, with many elk and deer. The people made their living by hunting and did not farm. They moved about without fixed habitations. All were fierce and skilled in fighting. They were called "Mountain Sheds."
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the Eastern Capital jurisdiction, where the land opens toward Deng and Guo, lie deep and sweeping valleys teeming with elk and deer. The people lived by hunting rather than farming, moved about without fixed homes, and were all swift, fierce, and skilled in combat. They were known as the "Mountain Sheds."

sentences.zh: 權德輿居守，將羈縻之，未克。

translations.literal: When Quan Deyu served as defender, he wished to win them over and keep them in check, but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Deyu had held the post of defender, he had tried to bring them under control but failed.

sentences.zh: 至是，元膺募為山河子弟，使衛宮城，詔可。

translations.literal: At this time Yuanying recruited them as local sons of the rivers and mountains and had them guard the palace city; the emperor approved by edict.
