translations.idiomatic: Now Yuanying recruited them as "sons of the mountains and rivers," assigning them to guard the palace city, and the emperor approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 改河中節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮多姑息，獨元膺秉正自將，監軍及中人往來者，無不嚴憚。

translations.literal: At that time most regional commanders were indulgent, but Yuanying alone upheld rectitude in his own command. Army supervisors and eunuchs who came and went—all were strictly restrained in his presence.
translations.idiomatic: In those days most regional commanders were indulgent toward their men, but Yuanying alone governed with upright discipline. Army supervisors and palace eunuchs who passed through his command all held him in strict awe.

sentences.zh: 入拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 正色立朝，有臺宰望，處事裁宜，人服其有禮。

translations.literal: With stern countenance he stood at court; he had the stature of a censor or chancellor; in handling affairs he judged appropriately; people admired his propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He stood at court with stern dignity, bearing the stature of a chief censor or chancellor. In handling affairs he judged each case on its merits, and all respected him for his propriety.

sentences.zh: 以疾改太子賓客。

translations.literal: Due to illness he was reassigned as Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to his reassignment as mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 居官始終無訾缺。

translations.literal: Throughout his tenure in office there was never any criticism of fault.
translations.idiomatic: From first appointment to last he served without a mark against his name.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously granted Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously granted the title of minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 許孟容，字公範，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Xu Mengrong, styled Gongfan, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengrong, styled Gongfan, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢進士異等，又第明經，調校書郎。

translations.literal: He was raised in the jinshi examination to exceptional rank; he also passed the Classicist examination and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination with exceptional distinction, also ranked in the Classicist examination, and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 辟武寧張建封府。

translations.literal: He was invited to serve in the headquarters of Zhang Jianfeng of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng of Wuning recruited him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 李納以兵拒境，建封遣使諭止，前後三輩往，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Li Na blocked the border with troops. Jianfeng sent envoys to advise him to stop; three missions went in succession, and none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na massed troops along the border. Jianfeng sent envoys urging him to withdraw; three missions went in succession, and Li Na ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 乃使孟容見納，敷引逆順，納即悔謝，為罷兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Mengrong to see Na, who set forth at length the logic of rebellion and loyalty. Na immediately repented and apologized, and withdrew his troops on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then sent Mengrong to see Li Na. Mengrong argued at length the logic of loyalty and rebellion, and Na at once expressed remorse, apologized, and withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 表為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Jianfeng memorialized to appoint him Prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng recommended him for appointment as prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗知其能，召拜禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong knew of his ability and summoned him to be appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong learned of his abilities and summoned him to serve as vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 公主子求補崇文生者，孟容固謂不可，主訴之，帝問狀，以著令對。

translations.literal: A princess's son sought appointment as a student at the Chongwen Academy. Mengrong firmly declared this impermissible. The princess appealed; the emperor asked the circumstances, and he answered by citing the established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When a princess's son sought a place at the Chongwen Academy, Mengrong firmly refused. The princess complained to the emperor, who asked what had happened, and Mengrong answered by citing the regulations on the books.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其守，擢郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his integrity and promoted him to Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his integrity and promoted him to director.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He rose in successive appointments to Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to become supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 京兆上言「好畤風雹害稼」，帝遣宦人覆視，不實，奪尹以下俸。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao administration reported that "wind and hail at Haoshi damaged the crops." The emperor dispatched a eunuch to verify; it was not true, and salaries were stripped from the prefect downward.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao administration reported that "wind and hail at Haoshi damaged the crops." The emperor dispatched a eunuch to verify; it was not true, and salaries were stripped from the prefect downward.

sentences.zh: 孟容曰：「府縣上事不實，罪應罰。

translations.literal: Mengrong said: "When prefectures and counties submit reports that are not true, punishment is warranted.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong said, "When a prefecture or county submits a false report, punishment is certainly warranted.

sentences.zh: 然陛下遣宦者覆視，紊綱紀。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty sends eunuchs to verify—this disrupts institutional order.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Your Majesty sends eunuchs to conduct such inquiries, the proper chain of command is thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 宜更擇御史一人參驗，乃可。」

translations.literal: It would be proper to select one censor instead to join in the verification—only then would it be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: It would be proper to select one censor instead to join in the verification—only then would it be acceptable."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 浙東觀察使裴肅諉判官齊總暴斂以厚獻，厭天子所欲。

translations.literal: Pei Su, Military Commissioner of Zhedong, shifted blame onto his aide Qi Zong for extortionate levies to make lavish gifts, satisfying what the Son of Heaven desired.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Su, commissioner of Zhedong, pinned the blame on his aide Qi Zong for extortionate levies used to make lavish gifts that satisfied the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 會肅卒，帝擢總自大理評事兼監察御史為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Su died, the emperor promoted Zong from Reviser of the Court of Judicial Review, concurrently Censor, to Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Su died, the emperor promoted Qi Zong—from reviser in the Court of Judicial Review, concurrently serving as censor—to prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衢，大州也。

translations.literal: Qu — a great prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou was a major prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孟容還制曰：「方用兵處，有不待次而擢者。

translations.literal: Mengrong returned the edict, saying: "In places where troops are deployed, there are those promoted without waiting their turn in the roster.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong sent the edict back, arguing: "In regions where armies are active, men are sometimes promoted out of turn—but that is the exception.

sentences.zh: 今衢不他虞，總無功越進超授，群議謂何？

translations.literal: Now Qu faces no other worries; Zong, without merit, receives a leapfrog supernumerary appointment—what will public discussion say?
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou faces no military threat, yet Zong is leapfrogged into a post he has not earned—what will the court and the realm make of that?

sentences.zh: 且總本判官，今詔書乃言『權知留後，攝都團練副使』，初無制授，尤不見其可。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zong was originally a judicial assistant; now the edict speaks of 'acting provisional governor in charge of affairs, concurrently administering the post of deputy military commissioner of the capital defense command'—there was never an initial formal appointment, which is especially unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zong was only a staff judge; the edict now calls him 'acting governor in charge of affairs, concurrently deputy military commissioner'—yet he was never formally appointed to either post in the first place, which is all the more indefensible.

sentences.zh: 假令總有可錄，宜暴課最，解中外之惑。」

translations.literal: Even if Zong had merits worth recording, his achievements should be made public and his performance ranked, to dispel confusion within and without the court."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zong had merits worth recording, his achievements should be made public and his performance ranked, to dispel confusion within and without the court."

sentences.zh: 會補闕王武陵等亦執爭，於是詔中停。

translations.literal: Supplemental Remonstrance Officer Wang Wuling and others also lodged objections, and so the edict was halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: Supplemental Remonstrance Officer Wang Wuling and others joined the protest, and the appointment was struck from the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝召謂曰：「使百執事皆如卿，朕何憂邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him and said: "If every official were like you, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him and said: "If every official were like you, what would I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 自袁高爭盧杞後，凡十八年，門下無議可否者。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Gao disputed Lu Qi, for eighteen years there had been no one under the Chancellery who debated whether edicts should pass or fail.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuan Gao had challenged the appointment of Lu Qi, eighteen years had passed without a single remonstrance from the Secretariat on whether an edict should stand.

sentences.zh: 至孟容數論駁，四方知天子開納多士，浩然想見其風。

translations.literal: When Mengrong repeatedly argued and rebutted, the four quarters learned that the Son of Heaven was open to receiving many scholars, and they yearned with high spirits to witness his manner of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mengrong began arguing edicts again and again, men across the realm saw that the throne was open to honest counsel, and they looked on with renewed hope.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年夏，大旱，上疏言：「陛下齋居損膳，具牲玉，走群望，而天意未答，豈豐歉有定，陰陽適然乎？

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of the Zhenyuan era, summer, there was a great drought. He submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has fasted and abstemious meals, prepared sacrificial animals and jade, and hurried to all the sacred mountains—yet Heaven has not yet responded. Could it be that abundance and scarcity are fixed, and Yin and Yang merely happen to align thus?
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, drought struck the land. He memorialized the throne: "Your Majesty has fasted, cut your meals, offered beasts and jade, and rushed prayers to every sacred peak—yet Heaven still withholds rain. Are harvest and famine truly fixed by fate, and yin and yang simply running their course?

sentences.zh: 竊惟天人交感之際，系教令順民與否。

translations.literal: I privately consider that when Heaven and humanity interact and respond to each other, it depends on whether edicts and commands accord with the people.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that when Heaven and men meet in mutual response, the hinge is whether the ruler's orders truly serve the people.

sentences.zh: 今戶部錢非度支歲計，本備緩急，若取一百萬緡代京兆一歲賦，則京圻無流亡，振災為福。

translations.literal: Now the Treasury funds are not part of the annual budget of the Directorate of Finance—they were originally set aside for emergencies. If one million strings of cash were taken to substitute for one year's tax levy of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture, then the capital region would have no displaced wanderers, and disaster relief would become a blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Treasury reserve is not part of the Finance Commission's annual budget; it exists for emergencies. Take one million strings of cash to cover one year's levy for the capital prefecture, and the capital districts would lose their refugees—turning disaster relief into a blessing.

sentences.zh: 又應省察流移征防當還未還，役作禁錮當釋未釋；

translations.literal: Further, there should be a review of those displaced by migration and frontier garrison troops who ought to return but have not, and corvee laborers and the imprisoned who ought to be released but have not been;
translations.idiomatic: The court should also review displaced persons and frontier garrison troops who should have been sent home but were not, and corvee laborers and prisoners who should have been freed but still languish in confinement;

sentences.zh: 負逋饋送，當免免之；

translations.literal: those in arrears on tribute and deliveries—where exemption is due, exempt them;
translations.idiomatic: those owing back taxes and tribute deliveries—where remission is owed, remit it;

sentences.zh: 沈滯郁抑，當伸伸之；

translations.literal: those stagnating in obscurity and repressed—where reinstatement is due, reinstate them;
translations.idiomatic: those buried in obscurity and crushed by injustice—where redress is owed, grant it;

sentences.zh: 以順人奉天。

translations.literal: so as to accord with the people and serve Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: so that the ruler may align with the people and thereby serve Heaven.

sentences.zh: 若是而神弗祐、歲弗稔，未之聞也。」

translations.literal: If this were done and the spirits still did not bless us, and the year still did not yield grain—I have never heard of such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: If this were done and the spirits still did not bless us, and the year still did not yield grain—I have never heard of such a thing."

sentences.zh: 先是，為裴延齡、李齊運流斥者，雖十年弗內移，故孟容因旱及之。

translations.literal: Earlier, those exiled and banished because of Pei Yanling and Li Qiyun—although ten years had passed, they had not been transferred back inward. Therefore Mengrong took advantage of the drought to bring this up.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, officials banished through the machinations of Pei Yanling and Li Qiyun had gone ten years without being recalled to the capital; Mengrong used the drought to raise their case as well.

sentences.zh: 帝始不悅，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: The Emperor was at first displeased and reassigned him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took offense at first and moved him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和初，再遷尚書右丞、京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, he was promoted again to Vice Director of the Right Department of the Ministry of Revenue and Metropolitan Governor of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanhe reign, he was promoted in succession to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Metropolitan Governor of the capital.

sentences.zh: 神策軍自興元後，日驕恣，府縣不能制。

translations.literal: Since Xingyuan, the Shence Army grew daily more arrogant and unrestrained, and the prefecture and county authorities could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: After the court's return from Xingyuan, the Shence Army grew more arrogant by the day, and neither prefecture nor county could restrain them.

sentences.zh: 軍吏李昱貸富人錢八百萬，三歲不肯歸。

translations.literal: The army clerk Li Yu borrowed eight million in cash from a wealthy man and for three years refused to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: An army clerk named Li Yu borrowed eight million cash from a wealthy man and for three years refused to pay it back.

sentences.zh: 孟容遣吏捕詰，與之期使償，曰：「不如期，且死！」

translations.literal: Mengrong sent officers to arrest and interrogate him, set him a deadline to repay, and said: "If you miss the deadline, you die!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong sent officers to arrest and interrogate him, set him a deadline to repay, and said: "If you miss the deadline, you die!"

sentences.zh: 一軍盡驚，訴於朝。

translations.literal: The entire army was alarmed and appealed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army was shaken, and the case was brought before the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲宗詔以昱付軍治之，再遣使，皆不聽，奏曰：「不奉詔，臣當誅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong ordered that Yu be handed over to the army for punishment. Mengrong sent envoys twice, but neither was obeyed. He submitted: "In disobeying the edict, your subject deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong ordered Yu turned over to the army for punishment. Mengrong sent messengers twice; both were ignored. He memorialized: "In defying the edict, I deserve death.

sentences.zh: 然臣職司輦轂，當為陛下抑豪強。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's duty is to govern the imperial capital region, and I ought to restrain the powerful for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my office governs the imperial capital, and it is my duty to hold the mighty in check for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 錢未盡輸，昱不可得。」

translations.literal: Until the money is fully paid in, Yu cannot be released."
translations.idiomatic: Until the money is fully paid in, Yu cannot be released."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其守正，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his uprightness and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his integrity and let him have his way.

sentences.zh: 京師豪右大震。

translations.literal: The powerful families of the capital were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The great families of the capital were thoroughly shaken.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 盜殺武元衡，孟容白宰相曰：「漢有一汲黯，奸臣寢謀。

translations.literal: Thieves assassinated Wu Yuanheng. Mengrong told the chief ministers: "In Han there was one Ji An, and treacherous ministers ceased their plots.
translations.idiomatic: When assassins killed Wu Yuanheng, Mengrong told the chancellors: "In Han times one Ji An was enough to make treacherous ministers abandon their schemes.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷無有過失，而狂賊敢爾，尚謂國有人乎？

translations.literal: Now the court has no faults, yet mad bandits dare do such a thing—can one still say the state has real men?
translations.idiomatic: The court has done nothing wrong, yet mad assassins dare strike like this—can we still say the realm has men of backbone?

sentences.zh: 願白天子，起裴中丞輔政，使主兵柄，索賊黨，罪人得矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty be informed: recall Vice Censor-in-Chief Pei to assist in governance, put him in charge of military authority, hunt down the bandit faction—and the guilty will be caught."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty be informed: recall Vice Censor-in-Chief Pei to assist in governance, put him in charge of military authority, hunt down the bandit faction—and the guilty will be caught."

sentences.zh: 後數日，果相度。

translations.literal: Several days later, Pei Du was indeed made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, Pei Du was indeed made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 俄以尚書左丞宣慰汴宋陳許河陽行營，拜東都留守。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter, as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, he was dispatched as imperial envoy to comfort the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang campaign headquarters, and appointed East Capital Defender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, he was sent as imperial envoy to the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang field commands, and appointed Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六，贈太子少保，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six. The throne posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and gave him the posthumous name Xian, "Principled."

sentences.zh: 孟容方勁有禮學，每所折衷，咸得其正。

translations.literal: Mengrong was upright and forceful, versed in ritual learning; in every judgment he balanced, he always hit the correct measure.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong was upright and resolute, steeped in ritual learning, and in every judgment he rendered he struck the fair middle ground.

sentences.zh: 好提腋士，天下清議上之。

translations.literal: He loved to lift up scholars, and the pure opinion of the realm ranked him highly.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in lifting up scholars, and men of public reputation across the realm held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 弟季同，始署西川韋臯府判官。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jitong first served as judicial assistant in Wei Gao's Western Chuan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jitong began as a staff judge in Wei Gao's Western Chuan command.

sentences.zh: 劉辟反，棄妻子歸，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, Jitong abandoned his wife and children and returned home. He was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rose in rebellion, Jitong left his wife and children behind and made his way home, where he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 歷長安令，再遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Chang'an and was twice promoted to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chang'an and was promoted twice to become a Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 孟容為禮部侍郎，徙季同京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When Mengrong was Vice Minister of Rites, Jitong was transferred to Deputy Metropolitan Governor of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Mengrong served as Vice Minister of Rites, Jitong was transferred to Deputy Metropolitan Governor of the capital.

sentences.zh: 時京兆尹元義方出為鄜坊觀察使，奏劾宰相李絳與季同舉進士為同年，才數月輒徙。

translations.literal: At the time, Metropolitan Governor Yuan Yifang was transferred out to be Regional Inspector of Bian-Fang. He memorialized accusing Chief Minister Li Jiang of having passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Jitong—yet within only a few months Jitong was transferred.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Metropolitan Governor Yuan Yifang was posted out as Regional Inspector of Bian-Fang, he memorialized accusing Chief Minister Li Jiang of favoritism: he and Jitong had passed the jinshi in the same year, yet within a few months Jitong was given a new post.

sentences.zh: 帝以問絳，絳曰：「進士、明經，歲大抵百人，吏部得官至千人，私謂為同年，本非親與舊也。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Li Jiang. Li Jiang said: "Each year the jinshi and mingjing graduates number roughly a hundred; over time the Ministry of Personnel raises as many as a thousand to office. People privately call them 'classmates of the same year'—but that was never a tie of kinship or long association.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned Li Jiang. Li Jiang replied: "Each year the jinshi and mingjing cohorts number about a hundred, yet over time the Ministry of Personnel may elevate a thousand men to office. People casually call them 'classmates of the same year,' but that is no bond of kinship or old friendship.

sentences.zh: 今季同以兄嫌徙少尹，豈臣所助邪？

translations.literal: Now Jitong was transferred to Deputy Metropolitan Governor because of his brother—how could that have been aided by me?
translations.idiomatic: Jitong was moved to Deputy Metropolitan Governor because of his brother's position—how could I have helped that along?

sentences.zh: 且忠臣事君，不以私害公，設有才，雖親舊當白用。

translations.literal: Moreover, a loyal minister serves his ruler and does not let private ties harm the public good. If someone has talent, even kin or old associates should be plainly recommended for use.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a loyal minister serves his ruler without letting private ties harm the public good. If a man has talent, even a relative or old friend ought to be openly recommended.

sentences.zh: 避嫌不用，乃臣下身謀，非天子用人意。」

translations.literal: Avoiding someone out of suspicion and not employing him—that is a minister scheming for his own safety, not the Son of Heaven's intent in appointing men."
translations.idiomatic: Avoiding someone out of suspicion and not employing him—that is a minister scheming for his own safety, not the Son of Heaven's intent in appointing men."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his explanation.

sentences.zh: 終宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Jitong ended his career as Regional Inspector of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Regional Inspector of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 薛存誠，字資明，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Cuncheng, style name Ziming, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, came from Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 中進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 擢累監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 元和初，討劉辟，郵傳事叢，詔以中人為館驛使，存誠以為害體甚，奏罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, when Liu Pi was being punished, postal relay affairs were piled up; an edict appointed eunuchs as postal station commissioners. Cuncheng believed this greatly harmed the body politic and memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign, as the court moved against Liu Pi, postal relay affairs fell into chaos. The emperor ordered eunuchs appointed as postal station commissioners. Cuncheng argued that this would grievously harm the state and memorialized to have the policy revoked.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中侍御史，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor and was promoted in succession to Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and eventually promoted to supervisor of attendants.

sentences.zh: 瓊林庫廣籍工徒，存誠曰：「此奸人羼名以避征役，不可許。」

translations.literal: The Qionglang Treasury broadly registered laborers and artisans. Cuncheng said: "These are wicked men who smuggle in names to avoid conscription — this must not be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: The Qionglang Treasury broadly registered laborers and artisans. Cuncheng said: "These are wicked men who smuggle in names to avoid conscription — this must not be permitted."

sentences.zh: 又神策軍與咸陽尉袁儋不平，誣奏之，儋被罰。

translations.literal: Again, the Shence Army and Xianyang magistrate Yuan Dan were on bad terms; they falsely memorialized against him, and Yuan was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence Army had a grudge against Yuan Dan, magistrate of Xianyang, and filed a false accusation against him; Yuan was punished.

sentences.zh: 二敕皆執不下。

translations.literal: On both edicts he held firm and would not issue them.
translations.idiomatic: On both edicts he held his ground and refused to promulgate them.

sentences.zh: 憲宗悅，遣使勞之，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was pleased, sent an envoy to commend him, and appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was delighted, sent an envoy to commend him, and appointed him vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 浮屠鑒虛者，自貞元中關通賂遺，倚宦豎為奸，會坐於頔、杜黃裳家事，逮捕下獄。

translations.literal: The Buddhist monk Jianxu, since the Zhenyuan era, had maintained contacts and bribery at the passes, relying on eunuchs to do evil. He happened to be implicated in the domestic affairs of Yu Di and Du Huangshang, was arrested and thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist monk Jianxu had since the Zhenyuan era maintained illicit contacts and bribe networks at the frontier passes, relying on eunuchs for his schemes. He became implicated in affairs involving Yu Di and Du Huangshang and was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 存誠窮劾之，得贓數十萬，當以大辟。

translations.literal: Cuncheng exhaustively investigated him and obtained bribes of several hundred thousand; he deserved the great penalty of death.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng pursued the investigation to the end and uncovered bribes totaling several hundred thousand cash; the punishment prescribed was death.

sentences.zh: 權近更保救於帝，有詔釋之，存誠不聽。

translations.literal: Those close to power repeatedly interceded with the emperor on his behalf; there was an edict to release him, but Cuncheng would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful at court repeatedly pleaded with the emperor on his behalf. An edict was issued to release him, but Cuncheng refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 明日，詔使詣臺諭曰：「朕須此囚面詰，非赦也。」

translations.literal: The next day, an edict envoy came to the censorate with instructions saying: "I need this prisoner for face-to-face interrogation — this is not a pardon."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, an edict envoy came to the censorate with instructions saying: "I need this prisoner for face-to-face interrogation — this is not a pardon."

sentences.zh: 存誠奏曰：「獄已具，陛下必欲召赦之，請先殺臣乃可。

translations.literal: Cuncheng memorialized saying: "The case is already complete. If Your Majesty insists on summoning and pardoning him, please kill me first — only then may it be done.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng memorialized in reply, "The case is closed. If Your Majesty insists on summoning and pardoning him, execute me first — only then will I comply.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, your servant dare not accept the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, your subject cannot obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 鑒虛卒抵死。

translations.literal: Jianxu in the end received death.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxu was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 江西監軍高重昌妄劾信州刺史李位謀反，追付仗內詰狀。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi army supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely accused Xinzhou prefect Li Wei of plotting rebellion; Li Wei was summoned and turned over to the inner palace guard for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongchang, the Jiangxi army supervisor, falsely accused Li Wei, prefect of Xinzhou, of plotting rebellion. Li Wei was seized and handed over to the inner palace guard for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 存誠一日三表，請付位御史臺。

translations.literal: Cuncheng three times in one day submitted memorials, requesting that Li Wei be turned over to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in a single day, asking that Li Wei be transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及按，果無實。

translations.literal: When the case was investigated, there truly was no substance to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was investigated, the accusation proved entirely groundless.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為給事中。

translations.literal: Before long, he again became Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed supervisor of attendants.

sentences.zh: 會御史中丞闕，帝謂宰相曰：「持憲無易存誠者。」

translations.literal: When the Vice Censor-in-Chief post was vacant, the emperor said to the chief ministers: "In upholding the law there is no one to replace Cuncheng."
translations.idiomatic: When the Vice Censor-in-Chief post was vacant, the emperor said to the chief ministers: "In upholding the law there is no one to replace Cuncheng."

sentences.zh: 乃復命之。

translations.literal: He thereupon reappointed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly reappointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 會暴卒，帝悼惜，贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he suddenly died. The emperor mourned and regretted it, posthumously granting him Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly soon afterward. The emperor grieved his loss and posthumously enfeoffed him as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 存誠性和易，於人無所不容，及當官，毅然不可奪。

translations.literal: Cuncheng's nature was gentle and easygoing; toward people he tolerated all, but once he held office he was resolute and could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Cuncheng was mild and accommodating toward everyone, yet once in office he was resolute and could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 子廷老。

translations.literal: His son was Tinglao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tinglao.

sentences.zh: 廷老，字商叟，及進士第，讜正有父風。

translations.literal: Tinglao, style name Shangsou, passed the jinshi examination and was upright and correct, having his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao, courtesy name Shangsou, passed the jinshi examination. He was forthright and upright, inheriting his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，為右拾遺。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era, he served as Reminder of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli reign he served as a remonstrance official on the right.

sentences.zh: 敬宗政日僻，嘗與舒元褒、李漢入閣論奏曰：「比除拜不由宰司擬進，恐綱紀浸壞，奸邪放肆。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong's government grew daily more wayward. Once, together with Shu Yuanbao and Li Han, he entered the inner hall to remonstrate, saying: "Recently appointments and dismissals have not come through the chief ministers' recommendations. I fear discipline will gradually collapse and the wicked will run riot."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong's government grew daily more wayward. Once, together with Shu Yuanbao and Li Han, he entered the inner hall to remonstrate, saying: "Recently appointments and dismissals have not come through the chief ministers' recommendations. I fear discipline will gradually collapse and the wicked will run riot."

sentences.zh: 帝厲語曰：「更論何事？」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke harshly: "What else do you discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "What else is there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: 元褒曰：「宮中興作太甚。」

translations.literal: Yuanbao said: "Construction within the palace is too extensive."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao replied, "Palace construction has become excessive."

sentences.zh: 帝色變，曰：「興作何所？」

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed and he said: "What construction?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "What construction?" he demanded.

sentences.zh: 元褒不能對。

translations.literal: Yuanbao could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao had no answer.

sentences.zh: 廷老曰：「臣等以諫為職，有聞即應論奏。

translations.literal: Tinglao said: "We take remonstrance as our duty; whatever we hear we ought to memorialize about at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao said, "Remonstrance is our duty. Whatever we hear, we ought to report it at once.

sentences.zh: 然見外輦材瓦絕多，知有所營。」

translations.literal: Yet we see an extraordinary abundance of building materials and tiles being transported outward, and know that construction is underway."
translations.idiomatic: Yet we see an extraordinary abundance of building materials and tiles being transported outward, and know that construction is underway."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已諭。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have been heard."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your point is taken."

sentences.zh: 時造清思院，殿中用銅鑒三千，薄金十萬餅，故廷老等懇言之。

translations.literal: At the time the Qingsi Courtyard was being built; in the halls three thousand bronze mirrors and one hundred thousand thin gold cakes were used — therefore Tinglao and the others spoke earnestly about it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Clear Reflections Courtyard was under construction, its halls consuming three thousand bronze mirrors and a hundred thousand thin gold ingots — which was why Tinglao and his colleagues spoke so earnestly.

sentences.zh: 尋加史館脩撰。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally appointed historiographer in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed a compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 鄭註用事，嶺南節度使鄭權附之，悉盜公庫寶貨輸註家為謝。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu held power, the Lingnan military governor Zheng Quan attached himself to him, plundering all the precious goods in the public treasury and sending them to Zhu's household as thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu came to power, Zheng Quan, military governor of Lingnan, attached himself to him, plundering the regional treasury of its precious goods and shipping them to Zhu's household as a gift of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 廷老表按權罪，由是中人切齒。

translations.literal: Tinglao submitted a memorial to investigate Quan's crimes; because of this the eunuchs gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao memorialized calling for an investigation of Quan's crimes. The eunuchs thereafter hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 又論李逢吉黨張權輿、程昔範不宜居諫爭官，逢吉怒。

translations.literal: He also argued that Li Fengji's partisans Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan were unfit to hold remonstrance offices, and Fengji was angry.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan, partisans of Li Fengji, were unfit for remonstrance posts. Fengji was furious.

sentences.zh: 會廷老告滿百日，出為臨晉令。

translations.literal: When Tinglao's mourning leave reached one hundred days, he was sent out as magistrate of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinglao's mourning leave reached the hundred-day mark, he was sent out as magistrate of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，召為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended, he was summoned as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, he was recalled and appointed palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 李讓夷數薦之，拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: Li Rangyi repeatedly recommended him, and he was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rangyi recommended him repeatedly, and he was appointed a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 日酣飲，不持檢操，帝不悅，並讓夷罷之。

translations.literal: He drank heavily every day and did not restrain his conduct; the emperor was displeased and dismissed both him and Rangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily every day and showed no self-restraint. The emperor was displeased and dismissed both him and Rangyi.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, he was transferred to Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Kaicheng reign, he was transferred to supervisor of attendants.

sentences.zh: 在公卿間，侃侃不幹虛譽，推為正人。

translations.literal: Among the high ministers he spoke forthrightly and did not pursue empty reputation; he was acclaimed as an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Among the high ministers he was frank and free of pretension, and was respected as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 子保遜，第進士，擢累給事中。

translations.literal: His son was Baoxun; he passed the jinshi examination and was promoted in succession to Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoxun passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive appointments to supervisor of attendants.

sentences.zh: 保遜子昭緯，乾寧中，至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Baoxun's son Zhaowei, during the Qianning era, reached Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun's son Zhaowei rose during the Qianning reign to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 性輕率，坐事貶磎州刺史。

translations.literal: His nature was frivolous and rash; because of an affair he was demoted to prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was rash by nature and, following a scandal, was demoted to prefect of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李遜，字友道，魏申公發之後，趙郡所謂申公房者，客居荊州。

translations.literal: Li Xun, style name Youdao, was a descendant of Wei Duke of Shen, Fa, of the so-called Duke of Shen branch of Zhao commandery, and lived as a client in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, courtesy name Youdao, descended from Li Fa, Duke of Shen of Wei, of the Shen Duke branch of Zhao — a lineage that had settled as clients in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 始署山南東道掌書記，累遷濠州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed recorder of Shannan East Circuit; through successive promotions he became prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He began as recorder to the Shannan East Circuit and rose through successive appointments to prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，濠州兵謀殺其將楊騰，騰走揚州，因滅騰家，曹亡剽劫。

translations.literal: Earlier, the soldiers of Hao Prefecture plotted to kill their commander Yang Teng. Teng fled to Yangzhou. In consequence Teng's household was destroyed, and scattered men turned to robbery and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the troops of Hao Prefecture had plotted to kill their commander Yang Teng. Teng fled to Yangzhou; his household was wiped out in the aftermath, and scattered men took to robbery and plunder.

sentences.zh: 遜至，鐫諭利害，眾釋鎧自歸。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, he earnestly explained the advantages and disadvantages; the multitude cast off their armor and surrendered of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun arrived, he earnestly explained what was at stake, and the men laid down their arms and surrendered of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 觀察使旨限外浮斂，遜一不應。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner ordered extralegal levies beyond the quotas; Xun refused every one.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner ordered levies beyond the statutory quotas, but Xun refused every one.

sentences.zh: 入為虞部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and became Director in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed Director in the Ministry of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 由衢州刺史以政最擢浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: From his post as prefect of Qu Prefecture, on account of the excellence of his governance he was promoted to observation commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as prefect of Qu Prefecture he was promoted, on the strength of outstanding governance, to observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 當貞元初，福建軍亂，前觀察使奏益兵三千屯於境，以折閩沖，遂為長戍，幾三十年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era the Fujian military rebelled. The previous observation commissioner memorialized to add three thousand troops garrisoned within the circuit to check Fujian's impetuosity; thus they became a long-term garrison, lasting nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era the Fujian army rebelled. The previous observation commissioner had memorialized for three thousand additional troops to be garrisoned within the circuit to check Fujian's aggressiveness; the posting became a permanent garrison lasting nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 遜署事，即停其兵。

translations.literal: When Xun assumed office, he immediately disbanded those troops.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Xun took office, he disbanded those troops.

sentences.zh: 入為給事中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and became Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 故事，天子以畸日聽政，對群臣。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Son of Heaven heard state affairs on irregular days and addressed the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, the emperor heard state affairs only on irregular days and addressed the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 遜奏：「陛下求治，而下有所陳，當不時上，豈宜限以日？

translations.literal: Xun memorialized: "Your Majesty seeks good governance. When those below have matters to present, they ought to submit them at any time—how can they be confined to certain days?
translations.idiomatic: Xun memorialized: "Your Majesty seeks good governance. When subjects below have matters to present, they ought to submit them at any time—not be confined to certain days, should they?

sentences.zh: 如是，畢歲得望天子者幾何？」

translations.literal: If it were so, in a whole year how many days would one get even to behold the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If it were so, in a whole year how many days would one get even to behold the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 憲宗悅，從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was pleased and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was pleased and accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 代嚴綬為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: He replaced Yan Shou as military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Yan Shou as military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時方討蔡，析山南東道為兩節度：以唐、鄧、隋三州授高霞寓，得專攻討，而遜督襄、復、郢、均、房五州賦饋之。

translations.literal: At the time the court was campaigning against Cai. Shannan East Circuit was split into two commands: Tang, Deng, and Sui prefectures were given to Gao Xiayu so he could mount a dedicated offensive, while Xun oversaw the tax levies and supply of the five prefectures Xiang, Fu, Ying, Jun, and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against Cai. Shannan East Circuit was divided into two commands: Tang, Deng, and Sui prefectures were assigned to Gao Xiayu for a dedicated offensive, while Xun supervised the tax levies and supply of the five prefectures of Xiang, Fu, Ying, Jun, and Fang.

sentences.zh: 初，襄陽兵隸霞寓者多逃還，後霞寓戰賊不勝，言為遜所橈。

translations.literal: At first many Xiangyang troops assigned to Xiayu deserted and returned. Later, when Xiayu failed to defeat the rebels in battle, he said Xun had obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: At first many Xiangyang troops under Xiayu's command deserted and returned home. Later, when Xiayu failed to defeat the rebels in battle, he claimed that Xun had obstructed him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲按狀，宰相請置不問，下遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to investigate the facts, but the chief ministers asked that the matter be dropped. Xun was demoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to investigate the matter, but the chief ministers asked that it be dropped. Xun was demoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 中人誣之，更貶恩王傅。

translations.literal: Eunuchs slandered him further, and he was again demoted to Tutor to the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs slandered him further, and he was demoted again to Tutor to the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 久乃歷京兆尹、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After a long interval he served successively as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and Grand Master of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he served in succession as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and Grand Master of the National University.

sentences.zh: 以檢校禮部尚書為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: With the titular rank of Minister of Rites he was made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: With the titular rank of Minister of Rites, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 時吳元濟始平，治條疏颣，遜召會大眾，申嚴約束，明諭賞罰，上下皆感畏，眾遂安。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Yuanji had only just been pacified; governance was lax and flawed. Xun summoned a general assembly, enforced strict discipline, and clearly explained rewards and punishments. Superiors and subordinates alike were awed into compliance, and the populace settled into order.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji had only just been pacified, and governance was slack and disorderly. Xun summoned a general assembly, enforced strict discipline, and clearly explained rewards and punishments. Superiors and subordinates alike were awed into compliance, and the people settled into order.

sentences.zh: 遜於為政，抑強植弱，貧富均一，所至有績可紀。

translations.literal: In administering government, Xun checked the strong and strengthened the weak, making rich and poor alike equal; wherever he served, his achievements were worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Xun checked the strong and strengthened the weak, treating rich and poor alike; wherever he served, his achievements were worth recording.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，幽、鎮繼亂，遜首建誅討計，不聽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing era Youzhou and Zhenzhou fell into successive rebellion. Xun was the first to propose a punitive campaign; the court did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing era, Youzhou and Zhenzhou fell into successive rebellion. Xun was the first to propose a punitive campaign, but the court did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以兵萬人會行營，即日上道，先諸軍至，由是進檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to rally at the field headquarters with ten thousand troops. He set out the same day and arrived ahead of the other armies. For this he was promoted to acting Minister of Civil Service Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to join the field headquarters with ten thousand troops. He set out the same day and arrived ahead of the other armies, and for this was promoted to acting Minister of Civil Service Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙節鳳翔，過京師，以疾求解為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to command Fengxiang. Passing through the capital, he petitioned on grounds of illness to be relieved and was made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to command Fengxiang. Passing through the capital, he petitioned on grounds of illness to be relieved of command and was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-three. Posthumously he was granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three. Posthumously he was granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子方玄，字景業，第進士。

translations.literal: His son Fang Xuan, courtesy name Jingye, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Xuan, courtesy name Jingye, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 裴誼奏署江西府判官。

translations.literal: Pei Yi memorialized and had him appointed judicial adjutant of the Jiangxi governor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi recommended him and had him appointed judicial adjutant of the Jiangxi governor's office.

sentences.zh: 有大獄，論死者十餘囚，方玄刺審其冤，悉平貸之。

translations.literal: There was a major case: more than ten prisoners had been sentenced to death. Fang Xuan investigated and found them innocent, and had them all acquitted and released.
translations.idiomatic: There was a major case in which more than ten prisoners had been sentenced to death. Fang Xuan investigated and found them innocent, and had them all acquitted and released.

sentences.zh: 累為池州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became prefect of Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became prefect of Chi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鉤檢戶籍，所以差量徭賦者，皆有科品程章，吏不得私。

translations.literal: In auditing household registers—by which corvée and tax assessments were determined—he established grades, categories, and fixed procedures so that clerks could not act on private whim.
translations.idiomatic: In auditing household registers—the basis for assessing corvée and tax obligations—he established grades, categories, and fixed procedures so that clerks could not act on private whim.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「沈約年八十，手寫簿書，蓋為此雲。」

translations.literal: He would often say: "When Shen Yue was eighty, he copied ledgers by hand—surely it was for reasons like this."
translations.idiomatic: He would often say: "When Shen Yue was eighty, he copied ledgers by hand—surely it was for reasons like this."

sentences.zh: 終處州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as prefect of Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遜弟建，字杓直，與兄俱客荊州。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, lived as a guest in Jingzhou together with his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, lived as a guest in Jingzhou together with his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 鄉人爭鬥，不詣府而詣建，平決無頗。

translations.literal: When fellow townspeople quarreled, they did not go to the magistrate's office but came to Jian, who settled disputes without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: When fellow townspeople quarreled, they did not go to the magistrate's office but came to Jian, who settled disputes without partiality.

sentences.zh: 母憐其孝，每字之曰：「㹻子勸吾食，吾輒飽；

translations.literal: His mother, taking pity on his filial devotion, would affectionately call him Wei-zi: "When my Wei-zi urges me to eat, I always feel sated;
translations.idiomatic: His mother, moved by his filial devotion, would affectionately call him Wei-zi: "When my dear boy urges me to eat, I always feel full;

sentences.zh: 進藥，吾意其瘳。」

translations.literal: when he brings me medicine, I believe I will recover."
translations.idiomatic: when he brings me medicine, I believe I will recover."

sentences.zh: 貞元中，補校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era he was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 德宗思得文學者，或以建聞，帝問左右，宰相鄭珣瑜曰：「臣為吏部時，當補校書者八人，它皆藉貴勢以請，建獨無有。」

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong wanted men of literary talent; someone mentioned Jian, and the emperor asked his attendants. Chief Minister Zheng Xunyu said: "When I served in the Ministry of Civil Service Affairs, eight collators were to be appointed. All the others relied on noble influence to petition for the posts; Jian alone sought none."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong wanted men of literary talent; someone mentioned Jian, and the emperor asked his attendants. Chief Minister Zheng Xunyu said: "When I served in the Ministry of Civil Service Affairs, eight collators were to be appointed. All the others relied on noble influence to petition for the posts; Jian alone sought none."

sentences.zh: 帝喜，擢左拾遺、翰林學士。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Reminder and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Reminder and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，李師古以兵侵曹州，建作詔諭還之，詞不假借。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Li Shigu sent troops to invade Caozhou. Jian drafted an edict summoning him back; the language brooked no softness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Li Shigu sent troops to invade Caozhou. Jian drafted an edict summoning him back, and the language brooked no concession.

sentences.zh: 王叔文欲更之，建不可。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen wanted to revise it; Jian refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen wanted to revise it, but Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 左除太子詹事，改殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was demoted to left-side appointment as Superintendent of the Heir Apparent's Household, then changed to Palace Censor Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Superintendent of the Heir Apparent's Household, then transferred to Palace Censor Within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 以兵部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: As Director in the Ministry of War he was entrusted with drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: As Director in the Ministry of War he was entrusted with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 宰相有竄定詔稿者，亟請解職，除京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When a chief minister tampered with a draft edict, Jian immediately petitioned to resign and was appointed Vice Governor of the Jingzhao metropolitan district.
translations.idiomatic: When a chief minister tampered with a draft edict, Jian immediately petitioned to resign and was appointed Vice Governor of the Jingzhao metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 會遜被讒，建申治之，出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xun fell victim to slander, Jian petitioned on his behalf for redress and was sent out as prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fell victim to slander, Jian petitioned on his behalf for redress and was sent out as prefect of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 初，建為學時，家苦貧。

translations.literal: In his early years, when Jian was a student, his family was desperately poor.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years, when Jian was a student, his family was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 兄造知其賢，為營丐，使成就之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zao knew his talent and arranged support for him, enabling him to complete his studies.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zao recognized his talent, arranged support for him, and saw him through his studies.

sentences.zh: 故遜、建皆舉進士。

translations.literal: Thus both Xun and Jian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Thus both Xun and Jian passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 後雖通顯，未嘗治垣屋，以清儉稱。

translations.literal: Later, though they rose to high office, they never repaired their walls and houses, and were known for purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though they rose to high office, they never repaired their walls and houses and were known for purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 建子訥，字敦止，及進士第。

translations.literal: Jian's son Ne, courtesy name Dunzhi, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Ne, whose courtesy name was Dunzhi, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 遷累中書舍人，為浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Secretariat Drafter and became commissioner for Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he reached Secretariat Drafter and became observation commissioner for Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 性疏卞，遇士不以禮，為下所逐，貶朗州刺史。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and harsh; he did not treat gentlemen with courtesy, was driven out by his subordinates, and was demoted to prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was blunt and harsh, treated gentlemen without courtesy, was driven out by his subordinates, and was demoted to prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為河南尹。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時久雨，洛暴漲，訥行水魏王堤，懼漂泊，疾馳去，水遂大毀民廬。

translations.literal: At the time prolonged rain caused the Luo River to rise violently. Ne was traveling along the Prince of Wei's embankment, feared being swept away, and galloped off in haste; the flood then greatly destroyed the people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rain had caused the Luo to rise violently. Ne was traveling along the Prince of Wei's embankment, feared being swept away, and galloped off in haste; the flood then destroyed many people's homes.

sentences.zh: 議者薄其材。

translations.literal: Commentators looked down on his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators looked down on his competence.

sentences.zh: 初，訥居與宰相楊收接，收欲市訥冗舍以廣第，訥叱曰：「先人舊廬，為權貴優笑地邪？」

translations.literal: Earlier, Ne's residence adjoined that of Chief Minister Yang Shou. Shou wished to buy Ne's spare quarters to enlarge his mansion. Ne rebuked him, saying: "Our forefathers' old dwelling—shall it become a place where the powerful come to jest and mock?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ne's residence adjoined that of Chief Minister Yang Shou. Shou wished to buy Ne's spare quarters to enlarge his mansion. Ne rebuked him, saying: "Our forefathers' old dwelling—shall it become a place where the powerful come to jest and mock?"

sentences.zh: 凡三為華州刺史，歷兵部尚書，以太子太傅卒。

translations.literal: He served three times as prefect of Hua, held the post of Minister of War, and died while Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served three times as prefect of Hua, rose to Minister of War, and died while Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遺命葬不請鹵簿，避贈謚，詔聽。

translations.literal: In his final instructions he ordered that his burial not request an imperial escort and that posthumous enfeoffment and an epithet be declined; an edict granted his wish.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he ordered that his burial not request an imperial escort and that posthumous enfeoffment and an epithet be declined; an edict granted his wish.
